children.translated_text: He who demonstrated to gods and men the path of suffering, its cause, cessation, and the way,

children.text: taṃ satpathajñaṃ praṇipatya buddhaṃ śāstraṃ kariṣyāmyabhidharmadīpam // Abhidh-d_1 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to that <s>Buddha</s>, the knower of the true path, I shall compose the treatise called <s>Abhidharmadīpa</s> (Light of Abhidharma). // Abhidh-d_1 //
If there is no change in <s>sattva</s> (being) and the rest, the non-manifestation of the manifest would follow;

since the modification (<s>vikāra</s>) belongs to that [<s>prakṛti</s>], the state of being modified would also belong to <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) due to its non-difference from it. // Abhidh-d_2 //
There is no action (<s>karma</s>) due to the self-abandonment of its own [nature]; the qualities of being known, manifest, and having a self are impurities;
in the first position there is no liberation, and in the second there are other calamities as well. // Abhidh-d_3 //
The <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form) consists of the eye and other [sense faculties]; it comprises ten <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) and <s>dhātus</s> (elements);
three <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are included in the one designated as <s>dharma</s>, together with <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifestation); and the three are permanent. // Abhidh-d_4 //
The one designated as <s>manas</s> (mind) and also the seven <s>vijñānadhātus</s> (consciousness elements);
<s>āyatana</s> (sense base) is explained as the gate of entry, and <s>dhātu</s> (element) is explained as lineage (<s>gotra</s>). // Abhidh-d_5 //
Due to suitability for practice, capacity, and other reasons, the Sage [<s>Buddha</s>] taught the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases),
and also the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements) for the sake of those who misconceive the intellect and other [factors] as a unity. // Abhidh-d_6 //
Since the six [consciousnesses] depend on another [faculty], that which is [their] cause is <s>manas</s> (mind);
because the substratum of both form and formless exists, the substrate of the five is declared to be material. // Abhidh-d_7 //
The inclusion of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) by their own nature is taught;
the equality of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitasīs</s> (mental factors) is due to their never being separated from their own nature. // Abhidh-d_8 //
Those that are designated by those names and stated in other <s>sūtras</s>, their inclusion in these [categories]
should be stated by one skilled in the method of the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), having considered their specific characteristics. // Abhidh-d_9 //
The mutual inclusion of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the rest should be understood in proper order;
permanent [entities] are not included in the <s>skandhas</s> because they do not fall into the [three] time periods and so forth. // Abhidh-d_10 //
The inclusion of the eighty thousand <s>dharmaskandhas</s> (aggregates of doctrine)
should be understood as being in the points of entry alone, since through them one enters the true path. // Abhidh-d_11 //
The measure of a <s>dharmaskandha</s> (aggregate of doctrine), however, is a single discourse on the truths and so forth;
but some hold its true nature to be speech, while others consider it to be name (<s>nāman</s>). // Abhidh-d_12 //
The fundamental basis for the designation of a being (<s>sattva</s>) is considered to be the six <s>dhātus</s> (elements);
since the conceit of 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>) ceases through the division of those [elements], they are taught. // Abhidh-d_13 //

children.text: kliṣṭameva hi vijñānaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ janmani śrayāt /
children.translated_text: Indeed, only defiled (<s>kliṣṭa</s>) consciousness should be observed at birth, due to the basis;
the space element (<s>khadhātu</s>) is distinct from <s>ākāśa</s> (space [as unconditioned]) because it is included in <s>rūpāyatana</s> (the sense base of form). // Abhidh-d_14 //

children.text: nabhaḥ khalu nabho dhātorāsanno hetureṣa tu /
children.translated_text: The sky (<s>nabhas</s>) is indeed close to the space element (<s>nabhodhātu</s>), but this is a cause

children.text: bhūtānāṃ tāni tajjasya rūpasyaitattu cetasaḥ // Abhidh-d_15 //
children.translated_text: of the [material] elements; those [elements are the cause] of the form born from them, and this [form born from elements is the cause] of mind. // Abhidh-d_15 //
That which functions through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), and that which [grasps] what has not yet been reached,
and that which [grasps] an object more distant than that, and that which is coarser than the others — // Abhidh-d_16 //
the first object [visible form] has visibility (<s>sanidarśana</s>); the ten that are material have resistance (<s>sapratigha</s>);

children.text: anyatra rūpaśabdābhyāṃ ta evāvyākṛtā matāḥ // Abhidh-d_17 //
children.translated_text: apart from visible form and sound, those very [ten] are considered <s>avyākṛta</s> (morally indeterminate). // Abhidh-d_17 //
The rest are threefold; here in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) all are fourteen;

children.text: rasagandhau savijñānau dhātū hitvā trayontimāḥ // Abhidh-d_18 //
children.translated_text: excluding taste, smell, and their [corresponding] consciousnesses as <s>dhātus</s>, the last three [remain]. // Abhidh-d_18 //
The last three are both with and without <s>āsravas</s> (outflows); the rest are with <s>āsravas</s>;
the first five have objects; three are with metaphorical [usage]; [they are] threefold. // Abhidh-d_19 //
They are non-conceptual, [grasping] the quality and the particular object, because they do not determine from <s>asmāra</s> and so forth;

children.text: manobhaumī smṛtiḥ pūrvo dvitīyo dhīrnirūpikā // Abhidh-d_20 //
children.translated_text: <s>smṛti</s> (memory) belongs to the mental ground; the first [type] is the second, which is discernment (<s>dhī</s>) that determines. // Abhidh-d_20 //
The five [types of] consciousness in the desire realm (<s>kāma</s>) are conceptual with one [kind of concept];

children.text: tasmādanyat tribhiḥ dhyāne prathame cāsamāhitam // Abhidh-d_21 //
children.translated_text: other than that, [consciousness] in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is with three [concepts] and also non-concentrated. // Abhidh-d_21 //
With two [it is] undistracted; with one [it has] eye, ear, and body as its basis;
with two it is distracted above that; with one alone it is concentrated. // Abhidh-d_22 //
For one whose wholesome seeds have been cut off, perception is conceptual;
there is no <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome) consciousness except at the moment of rebirth-linking (<s>pratisandhi</s>). // Abhidh-d_23 //
For the one who is free from desire (<s>vītarāga</s>) toward the sense realm, who is an ordinary person (<s>bāla</s>) with the nature of non-decline,

children.text: dvidhāpyakuśalaṃ nāsti kliṣṭaṃ cāryasya nottamam // Abhidh-d_24 //
children.translated_text: there is no <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome) [consciousness] in either way; and for the <s>ārya</s> (noble one), there is no supreme defiled [consciousness]. // Abhidh-d_24 //
There is no undefiled indeterminate [consciousness] that is conceptual belonging to a higher realm;
nor is there defiled conceptual [consciousness] that has a lower realm as its sphere. // Abhidh-d_25 //
Here [consciousness is] threefold for the <s>ārya</s> (noble one) who still has attachment and who possesses wholesome [qualities];

children.text: na śubhaṃ nāpi ca kliṣṭaṃ dvitīyādiṣu darśakam // Abhidh-d_26 //
children.translated_text: there is neither wholesome nor defiled perceptual [consciousness] in the second and higher [meditation levels]. // Abhidh-d_26 //
Through effort, through the proximity of conditions, through the homogeneity of the mental continuum,
<s>smṛti</s> (memory) arises in the mind regarding an object previously experienced by consciousness. // Abhidh-d_27 //
From the reverse of these [conditions], from dullness, from being overpowered by afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and illness,
forgetfulness arises regarding things previously known. // Abhidh-d_28 //
What has been seen by the mind in two, three, four, or five modes
is remembered by that [mind] and by the others; but one does not [remember] another's [experience], due to the cessation of incompatible perception. // Abhidh-d_29 //
What has been experienced by one of the five consciousnesses,
that is also remembered by another [consciousness]; and by that [consciousness], indeed, [what was experienced] by the others too. // Abhidh-d_30 //
That which is experienced by two types of indeterminate mind — here the twelve [types of mind] and so forth —
excluding the indeterminate of the form and formless realms, that is remembered by eight alone. // Abhidh-d_31 //
That which [is experienced] by the wholesome [minds] of the form and formless [realms] that have attained cessation, in sequence,

children.text: kāmāptāvyākṛte hitvā smaryate daśakena tat // Abhidh-d_32 //
children.translated_text: excluding the indeterminate attained in the desire realm, that is remembered by a group of ten. // Abhidh-d_32 //
That which in the form realm is seen by the indeterminate called 'unobstructed',

children.text: ārūpyāvyākṛte hitvā tadanyaiḥ smaryate punaḥ // Abhidh-d_33 //
children.translated_text: excluding the indeterminate of the formless realm, that is remembered by the others. // Abhidh-d_33 //
That which is known by the indeterminate of the formless realm — that by a group of nine,
excluding the indeterminate attained in the desire realm and the unobstructed attained in the form realm, likewise. // Abhidh-d_34 //
The seven designated as <s>citta</s> (mind) have objects; the one designated as <s>dharma</s> is associated [with mind];

children.text: amūrtā dhvaninā sārdhamanupāttāḥ nava dvidhā // Abhidh-d_35 //
children.translated_text: the immaterial ones, together with sound, are unappropriated; nine are twofold. // Abhidh-d_35 //

children.text: spṛśyaṃ dvidhā sadharmāṃśāḥ saha tā nava bhautikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The tangible is twofold; together with the <s>dharma</s> portion, those nine are derived from the elements (<s>bhautika</s>);

children.text: daśa sāvayavā mūrtāḥ ta eva daśa saṃcitāḥ // Abhidh-d_36 //
children.translated_text: ten have parts and are material; those very ten are accumulated. // Abhidh-d_36 //
Visible form, smell, taste, and touch are understood as having the nature of being both cutter and cuttable;
they are burners and weighers, and they themselves are also the burnable and the weighable. // Abhidh-d_37 //
Five have the nature of material <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties) and consist of the maturation of accumulation;

children.text: amūrtā naupacayikāḥ tridhā śeṣāḥ dhvanirdvidhā // Abhidh-d_38 //
children.translated_text: the immaterial ones are not of the nature of accumulation; the rest are threefold; sound is twofold. // Abhidh-d_38 //
The eye and the apprehension of that [visible form] — one may obtain them separately or together;
twelve are known as internal; the external ones consist of the six sense objects. // Abhidh-d_39 //
The last three are threefold; the rest are destroyed through the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>);

children.text: na rūpamasti dṛggheyaṃ nākliṣṭaṃ nāvikalpakam // Abhidh-d_40 //
children.translated_text: there is no <s>rūpa</s> (form) that is to be seen [and is also] undefiled and non-conceptual. // Abhidh-d_40 //
Only the homogeneous (<s>sabhāga</s>) is designated as <s>dharma</s>; the rest are taught as being of both kinds;
the homogeneous resembles its homogeneous counterpart with respect to its own function. // Abhidh-d_41 //
The eye, together with the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of dharma) portion, is said to be 'seeing' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) in nine ways;
the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) associated with the five [sense] consciousnesses is not 'seeing', because it does not determine. // Abhidh-d_42 //
Just as the eye sees the visible in cloudy and clear [skies], at night and during the day,
so too the defiled and undefiled [types of] seeing, and those of the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and the adept (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), see [in their respective ways]. // Abhidh-d_43 //
The eye sees; consciousness cognizes its own object;
since one is mere illumination and the other is apprehension, the difference between them is very great. // Abhidh-d_44 //
Is the effect of a single eye one consciousness, or of two [eyes]?

children.text: aprāpyārthaṃ manaścakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ca trīṇyato 'nyathā // Abhidh-d_45 //
children.translated_text: <s>manas</s> (mind), the eye, and the ear — these three [apprehend] without reaching the object; the others are otherwise. // Abhidh-d_45 //
Those that grasp without reaching [the object] are established because they grasp distant, near, and equal [objects];
if [one argues that] it is through the power of a lamp and so forth, [we reply] that is not equal, since it arises from that [same source]. // Abhidh-d_46 //
If [one argues] there would be the absurd consequence of grasping everything, [we reply] no, as seen from the case of the magnet and so forth;
if [one argues] there is no fault because [the faculty] pervades everywhere, [we reply] no, because there is no [invariable] connection, like sesame and oil. // Abhidh-d_47 //

children.text: na hyūrdhvaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ kāyo na rūpaṃ nākṣijaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body is not above the eye, nor is visible form, nor is the mind born from the eye;

children.text: vijñānasya tu netrārthastau ca kāyasya savaṃtaḥ // Abhidh-d_48 //
children.translated_text: but for consciousness, the eye and the visible object, and those two are everywhere with respect to the body. // Abhidh-d_48 //

children.text: nopariṣṭācchru teḥ kāyo na śabdo na svakaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body is not above the ear, nor is sound, nor is its own mind;

children.text: vijñānasya tu nihrādastau ca kāyasya sarvataḥ // Abhidh-d_49 //
children.translated_text: but for consciousness, [there is] the sound, and those two are everywhere with respect to the body. // Abhidh-d_49 //
For the three [senses of smell, taste, and touch], their own three [objects are present]; and for the body, consciousness also [operates] below;
but <s>manas</s> (mind) is unrestricted — this is shown as the mastery of the yogin. // Abhidh-d_50 //
The <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) that are with and without <s>āsravas</s> (outflows), those that are designated as <s>upādāna</s> (clinging),
should be known as being only with <s>āsravas</s>, due to their serving as allies [of the outflows], their function, and so forth. // Abhidh-d_51 //
The time periods and so forth are synonyms of <s>skandha</s> (aggregate); <s>dharma</s> and so forth [are synonyms] of an existent thing;

children.text: ye tu sāsravasaṃjñāste proktā duḥkhādināmabhiḥ // Abhidh-d_52 //
children.translated_text: those that bear the designation 'with <s>āsravas</s>' are expressed by the names <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) and so forth. // Abhidh-d_52 //
Due to the oneness of their own nature, sphere of activity, and effect, there is unity of <s>dhātu</s> (element);
even though the eye and other [faculties] are dual, there is a twofold derivation due to the threefoldness of action. // Abhidh-d_53 //
Due to the distinction of being uncommon, due to sovereignty, and due to being the inner [factor],
even though there are multiple causes, consciousness is differentiated by those [sense faculties]. // Abhidh-d_54 //
Because of its permanence and its being <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome), <s>nirvāṇa</s> is truly a substance (<s>dravya</s>);
by that essential substance, the single one designated as <s>dharma</s> is considered to possess substance. // Abhidh-d_55 //
The first pure <s>citta</s> (mind) is called a 'moment' (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) due to its lack of favorable conditions;
by that wondrous moment, the last three [consciousnesses] are momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>). // Abhidh-d_56 //
The nose, tongue, and body — these three grasp objects of equal [proximity];

children.text: paścimasyāśrayo 'tītaḥ pañcānāṃ taiḥ sahāpi ca // Abhidh-d_57 //
children.translated_text: the basis of the last [mind-consciousness] is past, and for the five [sense consciousnesses], it is simultaneous with those [bases]. // Abhidh-d_57 //
Depending on the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary meditation) or the four bases,
the eye element (<s>cakṣurdhātu</s>) is ceased through the <s>ānāsrava</s> (outflow-free) path. // Abhidh-d_58 //
Depending on the <s>anāgamya</s>, the odor element (<s>gandhadhātu</s>) is ceased;
the mind element (<s>manodhātu</s>) [is ceased] depending on <s>anāgamya</s> or on the seven bases. // Abhidh-d_59 //
Likewise <s>anāgamya</s> and the first [<s>dhyāna</s>] for that designated as the eye-consciousness [element];
due to the variegated nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of dharmas), one should specify according to the appropriate connection. // Abhidh-d_60 //
A <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person) who fully understands (<s>parijñā</s>) the eye element obtained in the form realm
attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) from the entire realm consisting of form. // Abhidh-d_61 //
Therefore, from that <s>dhātu</s> (element) one abandons thirty-one <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions),

children.text: paryādatte na kiñcittu saṃyojanamasau tadā // Abhidh-d_62 //
children.translated_text: but at that time one does not completely eliminate any <s>saṃyojana</s> (fetter). // Abhidh-d_62 //
One attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward form and abandons three <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions);

children.text: tadā saṃyojanaṃ tvāryaḥ paryādatte na kiñcana // Abhidh-d_63 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>ārya</s> (noble one) at that time does not completely eliminate any <s>saṃyojana</s> (fetter). // Abhidh-d_63 //
One who fully understands the eye-consciousness element also
necessarily fully understands that very [element] and becomes dispassionate from the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of Brahmā). // Abhidh-d_64 //

children.text: na tu saṃyojanaṃ kiñcitparyādatte tadā hyasau /
children.translated_text: But at that time one does not completely eliminate any <s>saṃyojana</s> (fetter);

children.text: gandhadhātuṃ rasākhyaṃ ca parijānan pṛthagjanaḥ // Abhidh-d_65 //
children.translated_text: a <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person) who fully understands the odor element (<s>gandhadhātu</s>) and the one called taste (<s>rasa</s>) // Abhidh-d_65 //
certainly attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward the desire realm and also [abandons] <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions);
at that time one abandons thirty-six and three current <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters). // Abhidh-d_66 //
But the <s>ārya</s> (noble one) accomplishes dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward the desire realm and also [abandons] <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions);

children.text: caturaḥ parijānāti paryādatte 'pi ca trayam // Abhidh-d_67 //
children.translated_text: one fully understands four and also completely eliminates three. // Abhidh-d_67 //
One who fully understands the mind element (<s>manodhātu</s>) becomes dispassionate from the formless realms;
one abandons thirty <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions) and likewise completely eliminates three. // Abhidh-d_68 //
One who fully understands joy (<s>prīti</s>) abandons that very [joy];

children.text: ābhāsvarācca vairāgyaṃ yāti hanti tu nāsravān // Abhidh-d_69 //
children.translated_text: and one attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) from <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (the Radiant heaven), but does not destroy the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows). // Abhidh-d_69 //
The yogin who fully understands pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) abandons that here as well,

children.text: śubhakṛtsnācca vairāgyaṃ yāti kleśānna hanti tu // Abhidh-d_70 //
children.translated_text: and attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) from <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (the heaven of Total Beauty), but does not destroy the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // Abhidh-d_70 //

children.text: dvivijñeyāḥ guṇāḥ pañca hetuḥ sarve kṣarākṣarāḥ /
children.translated_text: The five qualities are to be known as twofold; all are causes, perishable and imperishable;
except for half of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of dharmas), the six external [bases] do not have the nature of <s>indriyas</s> (faculties). // Abhidh-d_71 //
Of the complete twenty-two categories of the <s>indriya</s> (faculty) classification,
the <s>dharmas</s>, beginning with their etymological definitions, will be briefly explained. // Abhidh-d_72 //

children.text: nāmnā dvāviṃśatistāni dravyato daśa sapta ca /
children.translated_text: By name they are twenty-two; by substance (<s>dravya</s>) they are seventeen,
because the two [life and mind faculties] are not different from their effects, and the three groups of nine beginning with pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) [reduce to fewer]. // Abhidh-d_73 //
Because the name has no distinct defining characteristic, [it is established] from the meaningfulness of that name;
although the three [faculties of pleasure, pain, and indifference] function in groups, others seek a [further] meaning. // Abhidh-d_74 //
Due to being the cause of distinguished cognition, and due to the distinction of sovereignty,
the superiority [of the sense faculties] over the body faculty is [understood] for the two, like the eye faculty and so forth over [the body faculty]. // Abhidh-d_75 //
The meaning of <s>indriya</s> (faculty) is declared by the wise to be sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>);
for five [faculties], sovereignty is in their own specific functions; for four, it is in two domains. // Abhidh-d_76 //
Others know sovereignty as [consisting] in the initial apprehension of one's own object;
still others, who consider themselves learned, say it is only in the consciousness of one's own object. // Abhidh-d_77 //
In the arising of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), in the [faculties] of pleasure and so forth; in the attainment of qualities, in those of faith and so forth;
the sequence is due to their being [respectively] the fruit, defilement, accumulation, and purification. // Abhidh-d_78 //
By which [faculties] there is the designation of a being, the diversity of beings, sustenance, the arising of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the means to the path, and the attainment of the fruit — for those, the status of <s>indriya</s> (faculty) is accepted. // Abhidh-d_79 //
Fourteen [faculties exist] because of being the basis of contact (<s>sparśa</s>), arising, support, and enjoyment;
the other eight faculties exist because of being the cause of heaven and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). // Abhidh-d_80 //
Desire (<s>chanda</s>) and vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), because of being components [of the path]; contact (<s>sparśa</s>), because of nourishing feeling;
<s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), because of being overpowered by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — the Sage did not designate [these] as <s>indriyas</s> (faculties). // Abhidh-d_81 //

children.text: śraddhādīnāṃ vidāṃ caiva doṣaḥ śuddhau malodaye /
children.translated_text: For faith and the other [faculties], and for the knowers [faculties] as well, the fault [would arise] in purification and in the arising of defilements;
<s>manaskāra</s> (mental attention) is not designated as an <s>indriya</s> (faculty) because of being predominant [in all mental states]. // Abhidh-d_82 //
<s>Adhimokṣa</s> (resolve) also is not an <s>indriya</s> (faculty), because of being favorable to conviction.
<s>Cetanā</s> (volition) is not [the restraint] because of the doubt regarding the production of results at a later time. // Abhidh-d_83 //
Nor is <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness) that [restraint], since it is [subsumed under] <s>vīrya</s> (effort); nor is <s>hrī</s> (shame), because it [merely] restrains boldness;
nor is <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), nor <s>alobha</s> (non-greed), since they are overpowered by <s>vīrya</s> (effort) and <s>śraddhā</s> (faith). // Abhidh-d_84 //
Nor is <s>prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility) [the restraint], because it is [merely] the absence of agitation; nor are the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows), because they are blameworthy;

children.text: jātyādayo na pārārthyāt niṣkriyatvānna nirvṛtiḥ // Abhidh-d_85 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jāti</s> (birth) and so forth are not [the restraint] because they serve another's purpose; nor is <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation), because it is devoid of activity. // Abhidh-d_85 //

children.text: kāyasya bādhanaṃ duḥkhaṃ daurmanasyaṃ tu cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is the affliction of the body; <s>daurmanasya</s> (displeasure) is that of the mind;

children.text: sukhaṃ ca sumanastā ca sātaṃ śārīramānasam // Abhidh-d_86 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sukha</s> (pleasure) and <s>sumanastā</s> (mental satisfaction) are the agreeable [feelings] of body and mind respectively. // Abhidh-d_86 //

body.translated_text: On account of its excellence, the agreeable mental [feeling] is sometimes called <s>sukha</s> (pleasure). // Abhidh-d_87 //

children.translated_text: The <s>indriya</s> (faculty) beginning with the stainless one should be known as existing in six grounds;

children.text: tadanye nirmale tvakṣe draṣṭavye navabhūmike // Abhidh-d_88 //
children.translated_text: the others, however, should be regarded as belonging to nine grounds, being in the two pure <s>akṣas</s> (sense faculties). // Abhidh-d_88 //
<s>Daurmanasya</s> (displeasure) is to be abandoned in two ways; the three mental <s>vedanās</s> (feelings) [are abandoned] in three ways;

children.text: navābhyāsapraheyāṇi dvidhā pañca na tu trayam // Abhidh-d_89 //
children.translated_text: nine are to be abandoned through practice; five are of two kinds, but the [remaining] three are not. // Abhidh-d_89 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ kramodbhavaiḥ kāme vipāko labhyate dvayam /
children.translated_text: In the desire realm, through those arising in sequence previously, <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) is obtained as a pair;

children.text: anyaiḥ ṣaṭ sapta vāṣṭau vā ṣaḍ rūpe antye tu jīvitam // Abhidh-d_90 //
children.translated_text: by the others, six, seven, or eight; six in the form realm; but in the last, only the life [faculty]. // Abhidh-d_90 //
For those who are dying, three cease at the end; but eight in the intermediate [state];

children.text: daśāṣṭau nava catvāri kāme pañca śubhāni vā // Abhidh-d_91 //
children.translated_text: ten, eight, nine, four in the desire realm, or five wholesome ones. // Abhidh-d_91 //
The obtaining of the first and last [faculties] is with nine; and with seven or eight in the middle ones;
but the attainment [of faculties] is with eleven, due to the loss of the last fruit. // Abhidh-d_92 //

body.text: svasya dhātoḥ parijñānaṃ svavipakṣadṛśā pathā // Abhidh-d_93 //
body.translated_text: The full understanding of one's own <s>dhātu</s> (realm) is through the path that is the counterpart of one's own adversary. // Abhidh-d_93 //

children.translated_text: The full understanding of the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) is generally held to be through seven [faculties];
but with impure and pure [faculties] together, it is said to be through eight. // Abhidh-d_94 //
The full understanding of the <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) is held to be through ten <s>indriyas</s> (faculties);
the full understanding of the last <s>dhātu</s> (realm) is said to be through eleven. // Abhidh-d_95 //
All <s>sattvas</s> (beings) abiding in the three realms are endowed with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), life [faculty], and mind;
those in the desire realm [also have] touch, sex-characteristic, and [other physical] marks; those with form [also have] the eye and other [faculties]. // Abhidh-d_96 //
Indeed, one in the desire realm [possesses] the suffering [faculty]; one with attachment to it, the displeasure [faculty];
but one born in the upper [realms possesses] the pleasure [faculty]; the <s>ārya</s> (noble one) likewise [possesses] those called the pure, in the two lower [stages]. // Abhidh-d_97 //
One born in the two lower [heavens] possesses joy through what is called the pure; with the wholesome [faculties], that one has wholesome roots;
through the two <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) [faculties], those on the path of liberation; the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (non-learner), the <s>arhat</s>, has his own path [faculty]. // Abhidh-d_98 //
One endowed with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), life [faculty], and mind is necessarily possessed of [at least] three;
one with bodily pleasure, of four; and one with the eye [faculty], of five. // Abhidh-d_99 //
One endowed starting from the female faculty [possesses] eight; one with suffering is endowed with seven;
with eleven through the last two [faculties]; one possessing the first of those, with seven or six. // Abhidh-d_100 //
Those born in the three continents and the hells, even those fixed in wrong views,
possess at most nineteen and at fewest eight [faculties]. // Abhidh-d_101 //
Intermediate-state beings, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), animals, and <s>śraddhānusārins</s> (faith-followers)
are endowed with thirteen, or with nineteen. // Abhidh-d_102 //

children.text: samyaktvaniyatā ye tu ye ca śraddhādhimuktikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are fixed in right [view] and those who are <s>śraddhādhimuktikas</s> (conviction-liberated)
are endowed with eleven, or with nineteen. // Abhidh-d_103 //
The <s>arhat</s> called <s>prajñāvimukta</s> (wisdom-liberated), <s>kāyasākṣin</s> (body-witness), and <s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s> (both-ways-liberated)
possess eleven sense faculties, or are endowed with eighteen. // Abhidh-d_104 //
The deceased <s>Kāmadeva</s> (desire-realm gods) possess at fewest seventeen;
the same, at most, are endowed with nineteen faculties. // Abhidh-d_105 //
Those born in the two <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) possess at fewest fifteen;
those in <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (the heaven of Complete Purity) are endowed with fourteen. // Abhidh-d_106 //
Those in <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (the Great Fruit heaven) indeed possess at very fewest thirteen;
but these same, with all faculties at most, are endowed with sixteen. // Abhidh-d_107 //
Those in the formless realm possess at fewest eight and at most eleven;
beings [including] gods and <s>Kaurava</s> [continent dwellers] are endowed with thirteen. // Abhidh-d_108 //
One without the wholesome [faculties] is endowed with eight, or with thirteen;
those with dual sex-characteristics possess at fewest twenty, or at most twenty-one. // Abhidh-d_109 //
A <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom), which is externally situated, is indivisible into seven substances;
in the desire realm it has one additional [substance] in the body, and two additional in the eye and other [sense organs]. // Abhidh-d_110 //
The same should be understood in the form realm, except for the pair of smell and taste;

children.text: cittaṃ caitasikaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ tu svalakṣaṇaiḥ // Abhidh-d_111 //
children.translated_text: <s>Citta</s> (mind) together with <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors), and the conditioned [dharmas] with their own characteristics. // Abhidh-d_111 //
The ten <s>mahābhūmika dharmas</s> (universal mental factors) are: <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>cetanā</s> (volition), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness),
<s>chanda</s> (desire), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve), <s>dhī</s> (intellect), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>manaskṛti</s> (attention). // Abhidh-d_112 //
<s>Śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness), <s>prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility), <s>hrī</s> (shame), <s>apatrapā</s> (modesty),

the two roots [of non-greed and non-hatred], <s>vīrya</s> (effort), and <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-harming) — these ten are declared as the <s>śubhabhūmikas</s> (wholesome universal factors). // Abhidh-d_113 //
<s>Styāna</s> (torpor), <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness), <s>āśrāddha</s> (faithlessness), <s>ālasya</s> (laziness), <s>mūḍhi</s> (delusion), <s>uddhati</s> (restlessness) —

children.text: kliṣṭe ṣaṭ aśubhe tu dve āhrīkyamanapatrapā // Abhidh-d_114 //
children.translated_text: these six are in the defiled [universal]; and two in the unwholesome [universal]: <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness) and <s>anapatrapā</s> (lack of modesty). // Abhidh-d_114 //
<s>Māyā</s> (deceit), <s>śāṭhya</s> (guile), <s>mada</s> (pride), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>vihiṃsā</s> (malice), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), <s>pradāṣṭa</s> (hostility),
<s>sūkṣmopanāha</s> (resentment), <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) — these ten are the <s>parīttakleśabhūmikas</s> (limited unwholesome factors). // Abhidh-d_115 //
Just as a substance such as earth is qualified by qualities such as blue and so forth,
and is designated by various terms accordingly, so too the mind [is designated] based on its association with <s>caittas</s> (mental factors). // Abhidh-d_116 //
Just as the diversity of elements and derivative matter is not produced by their own nature here,
so too should the separateness of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors) be understood. // Abhidh-d_117 //
Just as a modification in water is observed due to contact with a related [substance],
so too should the modification of <s>cetas</s> (consciousness) be observed due to contact with associated [factors]. // Abhidh-d_118 //
'Quality,' 'qualifier,' '<s>dharma</s>,' 'measure,' 'mode,' and 'substrate' —
such terms and the like function with reference to a principal [entity]. // Abhidh-d_119 //
<s>Citta</s> (mind) is the principal among these, due to [its function of] grasping the mere object and so forth;
and this is also the seed of [all] activities, including purification and defilement. // Abhidh-d_120 //
The undefiled-indeterminate <s>citta</s> (mind) that has attained the desire realm arises together with twelve <s>dharmas</s>,
like the sun with its rays. // Abhidh-d_121 //
Likewise, the obscured [mind] arises with eighteen mental [factors];

children.text: dvāviṃśatyā sahāvaśyaṃ śubhaṃ bhavati mānasam // Abhidh-d_122 //
children.translated_text: the wholesome mental [state] necessarily occurs with twenty-two. // Abhidh-d_122 //
The unwholesome <s>citta</s> (mind) arises with twenty mental [factors];
that which is accompanied only by [wrong] view and delusion, one should state as having additional [factors] such as anger and so forth. // Abhidh-d_123 //
<s>Middha</s> (drowsiness) can occur everywhere; wherever it exists, it should be indicated there;
and likewise <s>kaukṛtya</s> (remorse) — one should count it as additional in some cases. // Abhidh-d_124 //
Unwholesome <s>middha</s> (drowsiness) and <s>kaukṛtya</s> (remorse) do not exist in the <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (form realm);
in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) [is absent], and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) also [is absent] above. // Abhidh-d_125 //
A <s>saṃskāra</s> (formation) that is associated [with mind] is one whose equality [with mind] is fivefold;

children.text: viprayuktaśca boddhavyaḥ samatā yasya nāstyasau // Abhidh-d_126 //
children.translated_text: and one that is dissociated should be understood as that which does not have this equality. // Abhidh-d_126 //
Because of the non-existence of distinguished [factors], there is no undue extension to material [dharmas];
and because of the inclusion [of the term] '<s>saṃskāra</s>' (formations), there is no undue extension to space and the like. // Abhidh-d_127 //
<s>Prāpti</s> (acquisition) and so forth are the thirteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) dissociated [from mind];
their marks are authoritative statement, own activity, and inferential sign — their characteristics will be explained. // Abhidh-d_128 //

body.translated_text: and of those born of hearing and reflection, and of the two <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments) — // Abhidh-d_130 //

children.translated_text: for the wholesome [dharmas] that are without defilement, conditioned, and unprecedented, [acquisition] of the defiled state

children.text: ādilābhe saha prākca tadūrdhvaṃ vā tridheṣyate // Abhidh-d_131 //
children.translated_text: at the initial obtaining is together with [dharma] and prior, or after that — it is held to be of three kinds. // Abhidh-d_131 //

children.text: kliṣṭāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ ca tadanyeṣāṃ tridhā matā /
children.translated_text: For defiled [dharmas], for wholesome [dharmas], and for others, [acquisition] is considered threefold;
likewise for obscured-indeterminate [dharmas], and for the minds of [supernormal] knowledge and magical creation. // Abhidh-d_132 //
At the initial obtaining of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is permanent, and of other [dharmas], always,

children.text: ajā tavartamānā ca kadācittu tridheṣyate // Abhidh-d_133 //
children.translated_text: the unborn and present [acquisition] — but sometimes it is held to be of three kinds. // Abhidh-d_133 //
That which is the cause of beings having the same goal and disposition is <s>sabhāgatā</s> (homogeneous similarity);
<s>Āsaṃjñika</s> (the state of non-perception) is the maturation in which mind and perception are cut off among those with perception. // Abhidh-d_134 //
The wholesome attainment of non-perception, which arrests <s>citta</s> (mind) in the last <s>dhyāna</s>,
is not attainable by the <s>ārya</s> (noble one), because it functions from the desire for escape; it is obtained through effort. // Abhidh-d_135 //
The one called <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) should be known as belonging to the summit of existence, for one who wishes to abandon [it];
it is wholesome, attainable through effort by the <s>ārya</s> (noble one), and is considered indeterminate with respect to two <s>vedanās</s> (feelings). // Abhidh-d_136 //
Because of the non-association with four kinds of <s>cetas</s> (consciousness), from authoritative tradition, and from reasoning,
and because of the state of mind being completely settled, this <s>acittikā</s> (mindless state) is established. // Abhidh-d_137 //
<s>Āyus</s> (life-force) is the basis for the designation of <s>gati</s> (destiny), the sustaining of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>uṣman</s> (heat);
from authoritative tradition and reasoning, it is held to be a real substance. // Abhidh-d_138 //
<s>Jāti</s> (birth), <s>sthiti</s> (duration), <s>jarā</s> (aging), and <s>nāśa</s> (destruction) — these are the fourfold marks of the conditioned;
four rather than [only] duration and destruction, because of the non-establishment of causality and so forth [otherwise]. // Abhidh-d_139 //
Aging is established through the loss of potency; it is not transformation due to being something other;
the loss of potency is established through the single effective action and destruction. // Abhidh-d_140 //
Given that birth exists, destruction too has a cause, because of the [subsequent] existence of that [destruction],
from the cessation of effective substance-action, from authoritative tradition, and from reasoning. // Abhidh-d_141 //
Those whose origination depends on vocal sounds, whose function is to convey their own meaning,
and which have names such as <s>saṃjñā</s> (name) and others — the three, namely <s>nāman</s> (name) and so forth, are recognized. // Abhidh-d_142 //
<s>Nāman</s> (name) and so forth are different from sound, because they illuminate meanings not [yet] apprehended;
they should be known as impermanent, because they manifest meaning dependently. // Abhidh-d_143 //
Sound, expressing its own nature, and syllables and so forth, are surely
that which conveys meaning — the wise one speaks of it as devotion and conceptual construction. // Abhidh-d_144 //
Because they are of the nature of <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms), the unity of sounds is not tenable;
identity [of sound and meaning] is [impossible] because of [sound's] resistive nature; this is established by obstruction and the like. // Abhidh-d_145 //
No other eternal sound called <s>sphoṭa</s> (meaning-bearing unit) is established apart from <s>ghoṣa</s> (audible sound);
by a sound occurring in sequence, no meaning is expressed [independently]. // Abhidh-d_146 //

children.text: na śrutyā śrūyate śabdastadanyā ca gatiḥ śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: Sound is not heard by hearing [itself], nor is there any other function of hearing;
whoever would assert [otherwise] would make himself a laughingstock among the learned. // Abhidh-d_147 //
What is to be illuminated, as appropriate, is both determinate and indeterminate;

children.text: niyatodbhāvanād buddhaḥ sarvajña iti gamyate // Abhidh-d_148 //
children.translated_text: because of the determinate manifestation [of all meanings], the <s>Buddha</s> is understood to be omniscient. // Abhidh-d_148 //
Those called <s>sattvākhya</s> (pertaining to beings) are obtained in the desire and form [realms], are outflow-indeterminate,

children.text: tathaiva ca vipākaśca sābhāgyaṃ prāptayo dvidhā // Abhidh-d_149 //
children.translated_text: and likewise maturation [acquisitions]; and <s>sābhāgya</s> (concordant) acquisitions are of two kinds. // Abhidh-d_149 //
There is no <s>sattvākhya</s> (being-designation) in the fourth [dhyāna] due to the absence of perturbation of beings, according to the <s>sūtra</s>;
since the vimāna (celestial abode) and its equality are destroyed, how can there be permanence? // Abhidh-d_150 //
Seven [destructions] by fire, then one by water; when the set of seven by water is complete, again
by fire [another] set of seven, and finally one wind-destruction. // Abhidh-d_151 //
After the set of seven by fire, one by wind — what follows next?
Due to the appropriation of lifespan, thus there is the increase of lifespan in <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (the Complete Purity heaven). // Abhidh-d_152 //
Because of the similarity to the faults of wind and so forth, those [cosmic destructions] destroy beings;
because of the resemblance to internal [bodily dissolution], [the earth-]destruction is not considered [separately]. // Abhidh-d_153 //
Of the causes that give rise to the rebirth of beings, which bring about misfortune and fortune,
<s>Karma</s> (action) is held to be the cause — the agent of the world's diversity. // Abhidh-d_154 //

children.text: kāyikaṃ vāṅmayaṃ caiva cetanākhyaṃ ca mānasam /
children.translated_text: Bodily, verbal, and mental — called <s>cetanā</s> (volition) —
these are the <s>karmas</s> (actions), the cause of the world; not <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and the like. // Abhidh-d_155 //
Because of the diversity [of the world], because of sequential arising, because of the undue consequence of [effects] being like [the supposed cause],
there is no dependence on another [creator]; and because of the faults of [fruitless] austerity, [arbitrary] connection, loss of thesis, and so forth. // Abhidh-d_156 //
The power of <s>karmas</s> (actions) is understood through injunction, time, apprehension, and so forth;

children.text: yato 'tasteṣu tācchabdyaṃ gauṇyā vṛttyā prayujyate // Abhidh-d_157 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the designation [of cetanā as karma] is applied to them by secondary usage. // Abhidh-d_157 //

body.text: pūrve vijñaptyavijñaptī cetanā mānasī kriyā // Abhidh-d_158 //
body.translated_text: The former two [types of karma] are <s>vijñapti</s> (intimation) and <s>avijñapti</s> (non-intimation); <s>cetanā</s> (volition) is the mental action. // Abhidh-d_158 //

children.translated_text: Just as food excessively burnt by fire, and a cooking pot that is [over-]heated,
so too is the <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline) of one with wrong views, whose self is damaged by guile, envy, and the like. // Abhidh-d_159 //
From the conventional [perspective], one endowed with right view [has] monkhood; from the ultimate [perspective],

children.text: ekasampattu saṃvṛtyā dvayābhāve dvidhāpi na // Abhidh-d_160 //
children.translated_text: there is one [type of] attainment conventionally, and in the absence of both, neither [type obtains]. // Abhidh-d_160 //
When the defilements have departed, in [pure] knowledge, the primary designation is by the word of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: tadāśraye phale cāpi vijñeyā guṇakalpanā // Abhidh-d_161 //
children.translated_text: and in the basis of that [knowledge] and in the fruit, the secondary designation should be understood. // Abhidh-d_161 //
Because of permanence and auspiciousness, and because of the cessation of all calamity,
<s>Dharma</s> is said to be <s>nirvāṇa</s> by primary designation, in that manner. // Abhidh-d_162 //
The <s>āryas</s> (noble ones), the qualities of the disciples — the <s>Saṃgha</s> is likewise [designated] in the ultimate sense;

children.text: etānyo yāti śaraṇaṃ sa yāti śaraṇatrayam // Abhidh-d_163 //
children.translated_text: one who goes to these for refuge, that one takes the threefold refuge. // Abhidh-d_163 //
Wrong conduct is condemned by the virtuous; because of obtaining [rebirth in a state] without [good] action in the next life;
false speech is the most sinful; drinking liquor, because of the destruction of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). // Abhidh-d_164 //
From all present [defilements] of both kinds, that which is born of the desire [realm arises];
but from the fundamental [defilements] of the three times, the two [restraints] born of meditation are obtained. // Abhidh-d_165 //
Restraint [is taken] from all classes of beings, through the causes of speech and body;

children.text: sarvebhyo saṃvarāṅgebhyaḥ sattvebhyaśca na kāraṇaiḥ // Abhidh-d_166 //
children.translated_text: from all components of restraint, and from beings — not [only] through [specific] causes. // Abhidh-d_166 //
The attainment of <s>saṃvara</s> (restraint) is through [ritual] action, or through [verbal] acceptance.
The other [<s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form)] differs by special features such as the field (<s>kṣetra</s>), limb, and so forth. // Abhidh-d_167 //
The abandonment of the <s>saṃvara</s> (restraint) obtained in the desire realm [occurs] through the renunciation of training (<s>śikṣā-nikṣepaṇa</s>) and the like.
Some say [it is lost] through a <s>pātanīya</s> (defeat-entailing offence); others say 'no' — because of [the absence of] disconnection. // Abhidh-d_168 //
[This is because] disconnection does not [occur] through the destruction of parts — [just as] the cloth-substance does not perish [when a thread is removed].
The statement of destruction in the <s>sūtra</s> has another meaning — as in [the cases of] envy, hypocrisy, and the like. // Abhidh-d_169 //
When the true <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared — others [arise]; others do not, since there is no first obtainment of what has not [previously] existed.

children.text: bhūsaṃcāreṇa hānyā ca tyajyate dhyānajaṃ śubham // Abhidh-d_170 //
children.translated_text: By moving to [another] land, and through loss, the wholesome [restraint] born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is abandoned. // Abhidh-d_170 //
Likewise, that obtained in the formless realm — but for a noble one (<s>ārya</s>), [it is abandoned] through attainment of the fruit, destruction of the faculties, and so forth.
Non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) [is abandoned] through attainment of discipline (<s>dama</s>), relinquishing of life, and the like. // Abhidh-d_171 //
But the intermediate <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form) [is lost] through the cessation of the intensity of mind and so forth.
What is called 'wholesome obtained in the desire realm' [is lost] through three [means]: cutting the roots [of good] and the like. // Abhidh-d_172 //
The afflicted [non-manifest] is destroyed through the arising of the antidote; [that] obtained in the three realms is destroyed.

children.text: sarve kāmeṣu rūpe dvāveko 'rūpiṣu lābhataḥ // Abhidh-d_173 //
children.translated_text: In the desire realm there are all [types]; in the form realm, two; in the formless realm, one — through attainment. // Abhidh-d_173 //
Whatever <s>karma</s> (action) gives the desired fruit is declared to be <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome).
The opposite [is] <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome); what is otherwise [is] <s>avyākṛta</s> (indeterminate). // Abhidh-d_174 //
The first, obtained in the desire realm, is <s>puṇya</s> (merit); <s>apuṇya</s> (demerit) consists of the unwholesome.
That belonging to the upper realms is <s>ānejya</s> (imperturbable) — because it does not waver with respect to its <s>vipāka</s> (retribution). // Abhidh-d_175 //
Wholesome <s>karma</s> from [the first] <s>dhyāna</s> up to but not including the fourth is to be experienced as pleasure (<s>sukha</s>).
Elsewhere [it is] to be experienced as equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>); but unwholesome [<s>karma</s> is] to be experienced as suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). // Abhidh-d_176 //
Even below [in the desire realm], intermediate <s>karma</s> [exists]; [even] in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, [it exists] for the sake of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation).
Because of the desirability of three <s>vipākas</s> (retributions) simultaneously — [this is possible] through retribution in an intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>. // Abhidh-d_177 //
Again, <s>karma</s> is fourfold according to the distinction of being experienced in this visible life (<s>dṛ���ṭa-vedya</s>) and so forth.
The projection of [a new] birth by three [lifetimes of <s>karma</s>], except that called 'to be experienced in this very life.' // Abhidh-d_178 //
And there is projection [of all types] by all four [kinds of <s>karma</s>] everywhere, except for the hells.
Because there is no desired fruit there, wholesome [<s>karma</s>] does not ripen [in hell]. // Abhidh-d_179 //

One who has performed <s>karma</s> 'to be experienced in the next birth' [is not reborn] there — [for] a common person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who is dispassionate [toward it is] stable, and a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) does not perform [new <s>karma</s>] for it.
Even an unstable one [does not go there] — at the root of the two [states of] existence. // Abhidh-d_180 //
When <s>karma</s> is repeatedly performed with a tender or fierce mind,

children.text: satkṣetre kriyate yacca phalaṃ tasya niyamyate // Abhidh-d_181 //
children.translated_text: and when it is done in a [meritorious] field (<s>kṣetra</s>) — its fruit is determined. // Abhidh-d_181 //
Due to the special features of the field and intention (<s>āśaya</s>), the fruit ripens immediately.
And immediately after arising from the cessation [attainment] and so forth, there is an immediate production of the time-fruit. // Abhidh-d_182 //
Because there is no re-arising in that plane — and whatever is determined regarding <s>vipāka</s> (retribution),

children.text: tacca dṛṣṭaphalaṃ vidyāt karmādaḥ paripūrakam // Abhidh-d_183 //
children.translated_text: that should be known as 'fruit visible [in this life]' (<s>dṛṣṭa-phala</s>) — [it is] the complementary <s>karma</s> [mentioned] below. // Abhidh-d_183 //
For wholesome [<s>karma</s>] that is non-deliberative, the feeling that is its <s>vipāka</s> (retribution) is purely mental (<s>caitasikī</s>).

children.text: vipākaḥ kāyikī tviṣṭā duḥkhavedyasya karmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_184 //
children.translated_text: But the desired physical (<s>kāyikī</s>) [feeling is the <s>vipāka</s>] of <s>karma</s> to be experienced as suffering. // Abhidh-d_184 //
The unwholesome together with its retribution is 'black' (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>); that born in the form realm together with its retribution is 'white' (<s>sita</s>).

children.text: śubhāśubhaṃ dvidhā kāme nirmalaṃ tatprahāṇakṛt // Abhidh-d_185 //
children.translated_text: In the desire realm, [<s>karma</s> is] twofold — wholesome and unwholesome; the 'stainless' (<s>nirmala</s>) is that which effects the abandonment of those [former types]. // Abhidh-d_185 //
Four paths of seeing (<s>dṛk-patha</s>) [exist] in the [path of] seeing: through the path of volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).
In the desire realm, the paths of the <s>ānantarya</s> (uninterrupted [path]) — this is the <s>karma</s> that destroys the 'black.' // Abhidh-d_186 //

children.text: navame cetanā yā tu sā kṛṣṇākṛṣṇayāghātinī /
children.translated_text: But the volition that is in the ninth [uninterrupted path] — that destroys both the black and non-black.

children.text: antānantaryamārgasthā dhyāne dhyāne sitasya tu // Abhidh-d_187 //
children.translated_text: Standing in the final uninterrupted path — but in each <s>dhyāna</s> [it destroys] the 'white.' // Abhidh-d_187 //
All unwholesome <s>karma</s> of body and the like is considered 'misconduct' (<s>duścarita</s>).
The three [beginning with] <s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) and the like are also the threefold mental misconduct. // Abhidh-d_188 //
The wholesome [counterpart] — beginning with non-covetousness (<s>anabhidhyā</s>) and the like — is declared as the threefold good conduct (<s>sucarita</s>).

children.text: dvayaṃmaulamadaḥ karma mārgā daśa śubhāśubhāḥ // Abhidh-d_189 //
children.translated_text: These two [sets] are the root; the <s>karma</s> below [is derivative]. Ten paths are [designated as] wholesome and unwholesome. // Abhidh-d_189 //
Six [of the ten paths] are caused [by another]; <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form) has two natures; one [is both]; those [six] are [also] 'performed' in six [ways].

children.text: śubhāḥ sapta dvidhā jñeyā ekadhaite samāhitāḥ // Abhidh-d_190 //
children.translated_text: The wholesome [paths] should be known as seven in two ways; [yet] in one way these are [all] concentrated. // Abhidh-d_190 //
The <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form) that [arises] in the preparatory [stages] — but in the subsequent [paths] the reverse.
The preparatory [action] arises from three roots; <s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) and the like are born from three roots. // Abhidh-d_191 //
The wholesome preparatory and subsequent [actions] are born from the three wholesome roots.
Through hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), the completion of killing, harsh speech, and malicious intent [is accomplished]. // Abhidh-d_192 //
Theft, going to another's wife — from greed (<s>lobha</s>); and <s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) as well [is from greed].
But wrong view (<s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s>) is from delusion (<s>moha</s>); for the others [it is] held [to arise] from all three [roots]. // Abhidh-d_193 //
The basis (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of [each of] the four [should be known] in order:

children.text: prāṇinaścātha bhogāśca nāmarūpaṃ ca nāma ca // Abhidh-d_194 //
children.translated_text: living beings, possessions, name-and-form, and name [alone]. // Abhidh-d_194 //
Taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) is the intentional killing of another, without error.
Taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>) is said to be the taking of another's property that has not been relinquished. // Abhidh-d_195 //
Sexual misconduct (<s>kāma-mithyācāra</s>) is going to another's wife — it has [many] variations.
Speaking otherwise than what is known, with intent to deceive — that is false speech (<s>mṛṣā-vacas</s>). // Abhidh-d_196 //
What is apprehended by sight, hearing, and the other senses, and what is grasped by the mind—

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mataṃ jñātamityuktaṃ tadyathākramam // Abhidh-d_197 //
children.translated_text: these are called in order: 'seen,' 'heard,' 'cognized,' and 'known.' // Abhidh-d_197 //
Divisive speech (<s>paiśunya</s>) is speech that causes division. Harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>) is what is unpleasant.
Idle talk (<s>saṃbhinna-lāpa</s>) is afflicted [speech]; others [define it] as songs, stories, and the like. // Abhidh-d_198 //
Covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) is desire for another's possessions. Malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) has sentient beings as its object—
hatred. Wrong view (<s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s>) is the view [that] the non-existent [is the cause], i.e., the denial of causes. // Abhidh-d_199 //
Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is not the action-path [itself]; but through those [action-paths], existence proceeds.
Simultaneously with up to eight unwholesome volitions, // Abhidh-d_200 //
but with wholesome ones, up to ten — together with one, eight, or five [mental factors].
Idle talk, hatred, and harsh speech occur in two [ways] in hell. // Abhidh-d_201 //
Likewise covetousness is considered [to occur]; and wrong view also similarly.
The triad beginning with covetousness likewise [occurs]; among the <s>Kurus</s>, idle talk [occurs] in two ways. // Abhidh-d_202 //
Elsewhere, [there are] ten unwholesome [paths]; the three wholesome [paths exist] everywhere.

children.text: ārūpyāryāsaṃjñināṃ ca rūpiṇaḥ sapta lābhataḥ // Abhidh-d_203 //
children.translated_text: For formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) noble ones and those in the <s>asaṃjñi</s> (non-percipient) [realm], those with form [have] seven through attainment. // Abhidh-d_203 //
Excluding the <s>Kurus</s> and the hells, elsewhere those [paths exist] in two ways.
All ten give <s>vipāka</s> (retribution), outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>), and dominant (<s>ādhipatya</s>) fruits. // Abhidh-d_204 //
From [<s>karma</s>] that terminates in suffering — suffering [results]; short lifespan from killing.
Emaciation and weakness from the destruction of vitality — this is the threefold fruit of that. // Abhidh-d_205 //
On the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantarya-patha</s>), <s>karma</s> bears fruit through five fruits.
But the stainless noble [path] through four; likewise other wholesome and unwholesome [<s>karma</s>]. // Abhidh-d_206 //
Different from that, the stainless [<s>karma</s>] should be known [to bear fruit] through three; indeterminate [<s>karma</s>] likewise.

children.text: phalaṃ śubhasya catvāri dve trīṇi ca śubhādayaḥ // Abhidh-d_207 //
children.translated_text: Wholesome [<s>karma</s> gives] four fruits; wholesome and the others [give] two, three, and so forth. // Abhidh-d_207 //

children.text: śubhādyāstvaśubhasya dve trīṇi catvāri ca kramāt /
children.translated_text: Wholesome and others [give] to the unwholesome two, three, and four in order.

children.text: avyākṛtasya te tu dve trīṇi trīṇi śubhādayaḥ // Abhidh-d_208 //
children.translated_text: For indeterminate [<s>karma</s>], those [give] two, three, and three — from wholesome and the others. // Abhidh-d_208 //
All [give] four [fruits] for the past [<s>karma</s>] and for the intermediate and the future [<s>karma</s>].
The intermediate [gives] two for itself alone; three for one not returning to [a new] birth. // Abhidh-d_209 //
Four [fruits for <s>karma</s>] of a single plane, or two, and three for [<s>karma</s> of] other planes.
Learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and others [give] three; the same three for learner's <s>karma</s>; those very [three] for the adept's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) <s>karma</s>. // Abhidh-d_210 //

children.text: ekaṃ trīṇi dvayaṃ caiva śaikṣādyāḥ paścimasya tu /
children.translated_text: One, three, and two — learners and others [give these for] the last [<s>karma</s>].

children.text: dve dve pañca yathāsaṃkhyaṃ dṛggheyasya tu karmaṇaḥ // Abhidh-d_211 //
children.translated_text: Two, two, and five respectively — for the <s>karma</s> to be abandoned by seeing (<s>dṛg-heya</s>). // Abhidh-d_211 //

children.text: trīṇi catvāri caikaṃ ca dṛṣṭiheyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Three, four, and one — those to be abandoned by seeing and others are recognized.

children.text: te tvabhyāsapraheyasya dve catvāri tridhā matāḥ // Abhidh-d_212 //
children.translated_text: Those [give] for the <s>karma</s> to be abandoned by cultivation: two, four, [and] three are held. // Abhidh-d_212 //
In order: one, two, four — those [give] for <s>karma</s> that is not to be abandoned.
By one [<s>karma</s>], a birth is projected; by many, it is completed. // Abhidh-d_213 //
Whatever <s>karma</s> — whether wholesome or unwholesome — that is past and [still] giving fruit,

children.text: svaṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarma sā karmasvakatā matā // Abhidh-d_214 //
children.translated_text: one's own <s>karma</s> of body, speech, and mind — that is understood as the 'ownership of <s>karma</s>' (<s>karma-svakatā</s>). // Abhidh-d_214 //
Conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtyā</s>), in the continuum of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), because action and fruit are observed therein,

children.text: kartṛtā bhoktṛtā coktā niṣiddhā śāśvatasya tu // Abhidh-d_215 //
children.translated_text: agency (<s>kartṛtā</s>) and experiencer-ship (<s>bhoktṛtā</s>) are stated; but the eternal [self] is denied. // Abhidh-d_215 //
'There is ownership of <s>karma</s>' and 'there is not' — this is the fourfold [set of propositions].
The first [is for one who] stands in the fruit of that [<s>karma</s>], through the loss of that <s>karma</s>. // Abhidh-d_216 //
The second [is for one who] stands in the fruit of that [<s>karma</s>] and is connected with that very <s>karma</s>.
The third [is for one] endowed with both; the fourth [is for one] with neither. // Abhidh-d_217 //
'There is ownership of <s>karma</s> [but] he will not experience its fruit'—
the first [proposition] should be known for one standing in its fruit, [understood] regarding the last fruit. // Abhidh-d_218 //
The second [is for <s>karma</s>] of certain retribution, when one does not stand in its <s>vipāka</s> (retribution).

children.text: tṛtīyā dvayasadbhāvā caturthī tūbhayaṃ vinā // Abhidh-d_219 //
children.translated_text: The third [is for] both existing; the fourth [is] without both. // Abhidh-d_219 //
'He is connected with <s>karma</s> and yet [there is] no experience of its fruit'—
the first [proposition is for <s>karma</s> whose] retribution has been given — [<s>karma</s> that is] ceased, future, and the like. // Abhidh-d_220 //
The second is for [one who is] devoid [of connection with <s>karma</s>] but [the <s>karma</s>] has certain retribution.

children.text: tṛtīyā dvayamuktasya caturthī tu dvayādṛte // Abhidh-d_221 //
children.translated_text: The third is for one free from both; the fourth is without both. // Abhidh-d_221 //
Improperly performed <s>karma</s>, corrupted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary defilements),
and [<s>karma</s>] devoid of training (<s>śikṣā</s>), marks (<s>liṅga</s>), and the like — some wise ones declare [such <s>karma</s> to be fruitless]. // Abhidh-d_222 //
From where [does one become] a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? From the time when, with irreversible mind,
he dons the armor of awakening (<s>bodhi-sannāha</s>), having undertaken the welfare of the world. // Abhidh-d_223 //
When he performs the <s>karma</s> that marks [him] (<s>lākṣaṇika karma</s>), not falling into lower realms,
[born in] a great family, with complete faculties, delighting in gathering his own assembly, // Abhidh-d_224 //
a male, remembering past births, eloquent, endowed with wisdom, vigor, and activity—
then he comes to manifestation among gods and humans. // Abhidh-d_225 //
For he, through three incalculable [aeons], accumulates the ocean of qualities of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body);

children.text: pracinoti tadādhāraṃ kāyaṃ kalpaśatena tu // Abhidh-d_226 //
children.translated_text: but the body that is its support — [he accumulates] in a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). // Abhidh-d_226 //
Endowed with the thirty-two marks (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>) and resplendent with eighty minor signs (<s>vyañjanas</s>)—

children.text: dviṣatāmapi yaṃ dṛṣṭvā manaḥ sadyaḥ prasīdati // Abhidh-d_227 //
children.translated_text: upon seeing which even enemies' minds are immediately gladdened. // Abhidh-d_227 //
By the wind at the end of an aeon, <s>Meru</s> [is destroyed]; by fire, the abode of <s>Varuṇa</s> (the ocean);

children.text: vajreṇa dhvasyate vajramavikāri tu tanmanaḥ // Abhidh-d_228 //
children.translated_text: by the thunderbolt, the thunderbolt [itself] is destroyed — but that [<s>Buddha</s>'s] mind is unalterable. // Abhidh-d_228 //
[That <s>karma</s>] obtained in the desire realm, born of the sixth [type], is threefold: [arising from] compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and one after another.

children.text: buddhotpāde naraḥ strī vā tadādyaṃ cittamaśnute // Abhidh-d_229 //
children.translated_text: When a <s>Buddha</s> arises, a man or woman attains that first <s>citta</s> (thought [of awakening]). // Abhidh-d_229 //
Giving everything, at all times, to everyone — this is the perfection of <s>dāna</s> (generosity).
Not abandoning discipline even at [the point of] death — this is declared the excellence of <s>śīla</s> (morality). // Abhidh-d_230 //

Of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), [the excellence is indicated] by the praise of <s>Tiṣya</s> [<s>Buddha</s>]; of <s>dhī</s> (wisdom), [the excellence is] beyond the <s>vajropama</s> (diamond-like [<s>samādhi</s>]).
'The perfection of all [<s>pāramitās</s>] is accomplished in the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣaya-jñāna</s>).' // Abhidh-d_231 //
The three bases of meritorious activity (<s>puṇya-kriyā-vastu</s>) and others — these are the teachings on the means of attaining those [perfections].
Likewise the four foundations (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) and the seven teachings of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>). // Abhidh-d_232 //
Seven unions (<s>yoga</s>), three aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), the three trainings (<s>śikṣā</s>), and others are taught.
Likewise the four <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>. // Abhidh-d_233 //
The thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) are proclaimed directly by the Self-born (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, i.e., the <s>Buddha</s>).
The causes of all awakened ones (<s>bodhi</s>) are threefold — according to mild [degree] and so forth. // Abhidh-d_234 //
Therefore, there is no path to awakening other than the three baskets (<s>piṭaka-traya</s>): <s>sūtra</s> and the others.
Whoever here should proclaim otherwise — he would be speaking the words of <s>Māra</s>. // Abhidh-d_235 //
This threefold <s>asaṃkhyeya</s> (incalculable) [period] is considered [to consist] of great <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).
Another position — [the number] called <s>asaṃkhyā</s> (incalculable) — is [a numeral] situated above that count. // Abhidh-d_236 //
A <s>Jina</s> (Buddha) arises during the decline [of human lifespan], as long as [lifespan is] one hundred years.
Of both [types of beings]: <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> [arise] during decline; <s>Cakravartins</s> [arise] during the increase [of lifespan]. // Abhidh-d_237 //
The arising of those [<s>Cakravartins</s>] is not held [to occur] below [a lifespan of] eighty thousand [years].
Their wheels are of gold, silver, or copper — through the power of merit. // Abhidh-d_238 //
Even when the means of practice are equal, the difference between those [results] is due to the difference of faculties and so forth—
like the difference in the fruit of giving for a mother [who seeks] liberation from existence and one [who seeks] [worldly] existence. // Abhidh-d_239 //
Due to the excess of the cultivation of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and likewise [the distinction between] one's own consciousness and the consciousness of others—
because the consciousness of others is more weighty [as an object] — that special distinction is established. // Abhidh-d_240 //
The greatness of the Teacher is threefold, arising from [the excellence of] cause, reality, and fruit.
Even when liberation is equal, [the distinction exists] because of the three [types of beings'] attainment of awakening. // Abhidh-d_241 //
In the presence of a <s>Buddha</s>, the buddhic body is projected.
Each mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of the Sage is produced from one hundred [acts of] merit. // Abhidh-d_242 //
Just as the action-paths [are classified], likewise the threefold [division of] merit and the rest is accepted.

children.text: dānaṃ hi dīyate yena svaparārthādyapekṣayā // Abhidh-d_243 //
children.translated_text: For <s>dāna</s> (giving) is that which is given with regard to one's own purpose, others' purpose, and so forth. // Abhidh-d_243 //
<s>Karma</s> of body and the like is its reality; <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest form) in some cases [is its reality].

children.text: prādhānyānmuninā proktaṃ mahābhogaphalaṃ hi tat // Abhidh-d_244 //
children.translated_text: The Sage declared it to be primarily [productive of] the fruit of great enjoyment (<s>mahābhoga</s>). // Abhidh-d_244 //
For accomplishing one's own, another's, or both purposes — some give <s>dāna</s> (gifts).
Others [give] for the sake of following virtuous conduct — not for both purposes. // Abhidh-d_245 //
From the excellence of the giver, the gift-substance, and the like — the excellence of the fruit is recognized.
The giver, endowed with virtues such as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the like, gives with respect, and so forth. // Abhidh-d_246 //
Therefore he obtains a fruit endowed with qualities of respect and the like.
A gift-substance endowed with color and so forth gives the fruit of beauty (<s>saurūpya</s>) and the like. // Abhidh-d_247 //
The field (<s>kṣetra</s>) is distinguished by [the recipient's] qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), [status as one in] suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), and helpfulness (<s>upakāra</s>).
From the mildness and the like of the intention (<s>āśaya</s>) [comes] the mildness and the like of the <s>karma</s>. // Abhidh-d_248 //
Giving to one who gives the <s>Dharma</s>, to a child, to one's father, to one's mother, or to one who is sick,
and to a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — that <s>dāna</s> (gift) is immeasurable; and also [giving] for the purpose of another existence. // Abhidh-d_249 //
That <s>dāna</s> (generosity) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — and also that which is the eighth [type] for another—
That which is declared by the wise as the best, from one worthy to another worthy one.
That which is undertaken after deliberation, made firm through fulfillment and the like,
and which is free from its antidote -- that <s>karma</s> (action) is considered accumulated.
The mental factors in worship of <s>caityas</s> (shrines) and the like depend on one's own renunciation and virtue;
even without a recipient, there is fruit, as in the case of abiding in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).
The gift of <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) has speech as its nature, with reality, names, and the like as its domain;
since it has an undesignated nature, it is not like the gift of food through names and the like.
<s>Śīla</s> (moral discipline) is a form consisting of what is wholesome; it has been explained according to its divisions.
But in the treatise, since it is predominant, it is declared to be for attaining heaven.
That which is not corrupted by faults such as immorality, unwholesome roots, and the like,
and which is a factor in the pacification of its opposite -- that is called <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline) here.
The <s>puṇya</s> (merit) that is concentrated here is <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), because of the cultivation of mind;
since it is predominant for liberation, it was declared thus by the All-Seeing One.
<s>Puṇya</s> (merit) is of the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-portion, and likewise conducive to penetration;
in this teaching, in brief, wholesome roots are said to be threefold.
Writing, seals, and calculation are characterized as bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> (action);
enumeration, however, should be known as having the nature of mental <s>karma</s> (action).
Because the world is inclined toward wrongdoing and partakes of suffering,
I shall now explain those <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) -- <s>rāga</s> (desire) and the rest -- which are the bonds of existence.
By names arising from activities produced by their own powers, these specific ones,
bearing general designations, are referred to as <s>anuśaya</s> (latent tendencies) and so forth.
<s>Rāga</s> (desire), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), <s>saṃmoha</s> (delusion), <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>kāṅkṣā</s> (doubt), and <s>kudṛṣṭi</s> (wrong views) --
these six are declared to be the <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies), which obstruct the doors to spiritual welfare.
Through the twofold division of <s>rāga</s> (desire), they are considered seven; through the division of views, they are remembered as ten;
furthermore, they should be known as ninety-eight through distinctions of realm, aspect, and the like.
<s>Kāma-rāga</s> (desire for sensuality) and that called <s>bhava</s> (existence) -- <s>rāga</s> (desire) is divided twofold,
mostly because of its outward engagement, and through distinctions such as inner and the like.
The grasping of the existing body, the grasping of the two extremes, wrong view itself,
and the clinging to rites and rituals -- these are the five <s>dṛṣṭis</s> (views).
Ten are to be abandoned by the insight into suffering; seven are destroyed by the vision of the cause;
seven are to be abandoned by the insight into cessation; eight are destroyed by the vision of the path.
Because they depend on what is to be abandoned by insight, and because they constantly apprehend their aspects,
but <s>rāga</s> (desire) and the other four should be known as destroyed by both types of path.
Because they arise under the influence of each conceptual construction, doubt and views are abandoned by the destruction of insight;
likewise in the form realm, and in the formless realm, except for the <s>pratigha</s> (aversion) latent tendency.

children.text: bhavāgre kṣāntiheyā ye dṛggheyā eva te matāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those in <s>Bhavāgra</s> (the Peak of Existence) that are to be abandoned by <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) are considered to be abandoned by insight alone;
but those to be killed by <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) there -- their destruction is through repeated practice alone.

children.text: ahaṃ mameti yā dṛṣṭirasau satkāyadṛk smṛtā /
children.translated_text: The view which grasps 'I' and 'mine' is remembered as <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body);
the grasping of its annihilation and permanence -- that is considered the view of grasping the extremes.
That which denies the fruit and the cause is called <s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view);
<s>dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa</s> (clinging to views) should be known as the grasping of an inferior thing as superior.
And in what is not a cause or not a path, that indeed is called <s>śīla-vrata</s> (clinging to rites and rituals);
because of adopting a wrong path through confusion about suffering, it is to be set aside through that insight.
The cutting off of <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body) is because one sees only <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena),
and that occurs in the <s>abhisamaya</s> (comprehension) of suffering; therefore that too is to be abandoned by insight alone.
Two <s>viparyāsas</s> (distortions) arise from <s>dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa</s> (clinging to views), one from <s>satkāya-dṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body),
and another is conceived from half of the extreme-grasping view -- thus the <s>viparyāsa</s> (distortion) is formulated.
Because of the perverted engagement of non-ascertainment and superimposition,
the statement of <s>viparyāsa</s> (distortion) applies to these alone, due to view, in the categories of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception).
Seven kinds of <s>māna</s> (pride) arise from three; nine kinds of <s>māna</s> (pride) arise threefold,
from the three realms, through self-exaltation and the like -- there is the assertion and denial of one's own superiority and so on.
The mental states of killing and the like, <s>kaukṛtya</s> (remorse), unwholesome dispositions,

children.text: vibhavecchā ca nāryasya jāyante hetvabhāvataḥ // Abhidh-d_276 //
children.translated_text: and the desire for annihilation -- these of the ignoble one arise from the absence of a cause.
From suffering and from its origination is the establishment of the universals;
of all those classes to be abandoned by insight, this is because of their standing on two bases.
Doubt, the five views, and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) -- whether mixed with those or alone --
seven are universal from suffering; from the cause, a group of four.

children.text: dravyato daśa caikaśca nāmnā sapta tu te matāḥ /
children.translated_text: In substance they are eleven, but by name they are considered seven;
<s>rāga</s> (desire), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>māna</s> (pride), however, operate within their own domain.
Because of operating in a different manner, the universal one pervades all grounds at once;
because of depending on another realm, those mentioned earlier are indeed the universals.
Nine belong to the upper realms; among them, the first two views are excluded;

children.text: teṣāṃ sahabhuvo dharmāḥ prāptivarjyāśca sarvagāḥ // Abhidh-d_281 //
children.translated_text: the <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) co-existent with them, excluding <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition), are also universal.
Doubt, <s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view), mixed <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and also the isolated one --
these six, to be abandoned by the insight into cessation and the path, are the ones discerned by the pure.
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> (cessation) pertains to one's own ground alone; the path, however, relates to the nine grounds;
the objects seen by that insight are different from each other, because of being a cause and because of the state of being a cause.
There is no <s>rāga</s> (desire), because power is not a cause; no <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), because there is no offense;
no <s>māna</s> (pride), because of extreme tranquility; and no other views, because of their nature as entities.
A universal <s>anuśaya</s> (latent tendency), belonging to its own realm, underlies the entire
ground as its object; but a non-universal one underlies only its own class.
Because of non-acceptance and because of being an antidote, it does not take as its object the higher ground or path;
but regarding what is associated with it, the association is with what is not inferior to itself.
By the analogies of the nurse, cloth, and dirt, and by the sequence of those moving in sky and water,
since these underlie, therefore they are remembered as <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies).
Through their own desired and other aspects, even in the smallest atoms and moments,
since these underlie, therefore they are considered <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies).
The first pair of views in the desire realm is considered as obstructed-indeterminate;

children.text: dhātudvaye tu sarve 'pi nivṛtāvyākṛtā malāḥ // Abhidh-d_289 //
children.translated_text: in the two higher realms, however, all defilements are obstructed-indeterminate.
The remaining ones in the desire realm are unwholesome, because of <s>rāga</s> (desire), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>tamas</s> (darkness);
there are only three unwholesome roots, by the conjunction of five reasons.
Even for the two types of indeterminate, there are three roots, being similar to those;

children.text: avidyā dhīśca tṛṣṇā ca na kāṅkṣāmānadṛṣṭayaḥ // Abhidh-d_291 //
children.translated_text: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), understanding, and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) -- but not doubt, pride, or views.
Because of instability, because of functioning in the upper realms, and because of non-pervasiveness, respectively;
from not understanding the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>, and from the objection of one who contemplates without a cause.
The Best of Speakers declared four types of answering questions,

children.text: śiṣyāṇāṃ vādaśikṣārthaṃ sthitīnāṃ ca catuṣṭayīm // Abhidh-d_293 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of training disciples in debate, and a fourfold set of positions.
The categorical statement, the analytical statement, the counter-question, and the setting aside --
as in cases of death, birth, excellence, and the identity of the living being and the body, and so on.
One designation is that of the positionist; another is called the conceptualist;
another is called the methodologist; and another is designated the knowledgist.
One who is engaged through <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>rāga</s> (attachment), with actions not yet relinquished --
wherever they have arisen and are not abandoned, one is bound to that object.
By these mental ones that have not yet arisen, everywhere by others belonging to one's own time-period,
everywhere by those not yet born, and likewise by the remaining ones -- the aggregate-continuum is bound.
Only two are established here in the primary sense; the third is through metaphorical usage,
because of being a cause of both the existent and the non-existent, and because of being accepted by the neutral ones.
