'Everything exists' is one position; 'a part exists' is another; 'nothing exists' says yet another;
'the indeterminate exists' -- thus four types of proponents are remembered.

children.text: ebhyo yaḥ prathamo vādī bhajate sādhutāmasau /
children.translated_text: Among these, the first proponent attains correctness;
the others, who pride themselves on reasoning, are excluded from both logic and scripture.
Because he accepts the three time-periods, and because of the permanence of the three through function,
he is called a <s>Sarvāstivādin</s> (proponent of 'everything exists') -- the first of the four types.
Two are called the proponents of otherness of nature and of state;
another is the proponent of otherness in a different sense -- the third speaks through reasoning.
He wishes to establish the distinction of time-periods through causal efficacy;
that which is performing its function is the present time-period; when it has performed, it is past; when it has not, it is future.
That whose characteristic is perceived by the intellect is to be cognized -- it is fourfold:
in the ultimate sense, in the conventional sense, through both, and also through relative designation.
The past is existent as not-yet-arisen, like the present, according to the <s>Buddha's</s> statement;
and because of not being beyond the range of cognitions, its existence is like that of the present.
Cognition does not have the non-existent as its object, based on scripture and reasoning;
and regarding the relatively designated, the denial of relation applies to the horns of a horse.
When a material object and so forth has perished, cognition arises while it still exists;
that cognition bears the aspect of its object, like the <s>Buddha's</s> knowledge of another's mind.
Because of the arising of joy, fear, agitation, and memory, and because of being a factor thereof,
the manifestation of the power of what possesses its factors -- like a lamp, a pot, and a form.
The agent of production accomplishes what is to be accomplished, like the five modifications of existence;
because action is seen as a factor of what exists, like the action of modifying and attaining.
A second birth does not occur for an entity that has already been born;

children.text: mukhyasattā guṇābhāvādgauṇī sattā na vidyate // Abhidh-d_310 //
children.translated_text: primary existence is absent due to lack of qualities; secondary existence is not found.
When there is similarity in properties, the usage of that obtains, like the expression 'sweet';
the birth of the primary, with its characteristic manifest, is accepted as in the case of a child and the like.
The sky would be blossoming with sky-flowers, and the frog would have matted locks,

children.text: svabhāvo yadi bhāvanāṃ prāgabhūtvā samudbhavet // Abhidh-d_312 //
children.translated_text: if the intrinsic nature of things were to arise having previously not existed.
Entities that are devoid of the power of persistence, whose arising is accompanied by destruction --

children.text: vada somya kathaṃ yāti pratītyā vastu vastutām // Abhidh-d_313 //
children.translated_text: tell me, dear one, how does an entity come to be an entity through dependent origination?
In the world, mutual assistance is observed only among what exists;
likewise mutual harm -- not of the horns of a horse or the feet of a snake.
What has arisen through dependent origination does not exist by its own nature;
that which does not exist by its own nature -- if it does not exist, then it is otherwise than that.
Causes produce merely a change of state in an entity that exists;
like the ministers make the prince into a king, one who already has a self.
When there is an assemblage of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), a capacity arises,
just as with accumulated atoms in the apprehension of a self.
If one's past <s>karma</s> (action) is non-existent, then the future fruit it produces is also non-existent;
clearly, the son of a barren woman would be born from an inter-being offspring.
Since a name lacks a real characteristic, and since the reality of substance is established through its marks,
the future and the past do not have merely conventional existence.

children.text: ko vighnaḥ aṅgavaikalyam na tatsarvāstitā sadā /
children.translated_text: What is the obstacle? It is the deficiency of factors. That does not mean that everything always exists;

children.text: tatkathaṃ śrūyatāṃ sadbhyaḥ durbodhā khalu dharmatā // Abhidh-d_320 //
children.translated_text: then how? Listen from the good: the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is indeed difficult to comprehend.
From the conjunction with the present time-period, from the acquisition of the factors of the assemblage,
the projection of fruit by one who has obtained the power -- that is called causal efficacy.
Being-present is not a form, nor is being-past or being-future;
therefore, not through passage through time-periods -- the nature of form is considered to be otherwise.
A certain state arises in an existing entity;

children.text: tathā śaktistathā velā tathā sattā tathā kriyā // Abhidh-d_323 //
children.translated_text: likewise a power, likewise a time, likewise an existence, likewise an activity.
The world is pervaded by conceptual constructions that delight the minds of the foolish;

children.text: yastu vidvanmanogrāhī parikalpaḥ sa durlabhaḥ // Abhidh-d_324 //
children.translated_text: but that conceptual construction which grasps the mind of the wise is rare.
When the destruction through the insight into suffering of those bound by other universals has been accomplished,
even when the earlier type has been abandoned, one is still bound by the remaining ones that depend on it.
Sixteen <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) should be known, each having the nature of the three realms of existence,

children.text: pañcadhā nirmalāścaiva vijñānāni tathaiva ca // Abhidh-d_326 //
children.translated_text: and they are fivefold as pure, and likewise the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses).
One should discern them with respect to elements, sense-bases, truths,
and modes -- as prompted by the collection of <s>dharmas</s>, consciousness, knowledge, and latent tendencies.
Those to be abandoned by the insight into suffering and its cause, those attained in the desire realm, those destroyed by meditation,
those attaining a single form through their own three, the dispassionate ones, and those in the domain of mind.
Those born from form through their own three and one above, belonging to the self;
those attained in the formless realm, those attaining the three realms, and those in the domain of the triple pure.
All should be known as their own and higher; those destroyed by the insight into the path of liberation together,
those free from defilements, attaining the three realms of existence, and those in the domain of the last three pures.
That attained in the desire realm has five objects; that attained in the form realm has eight objects;

children.text: ārupyāptaṃ daśānāṃ tu daśānāmeva cāmalam // Abhidh-d_331 //
children.translated_text: that attained in the formless realm has ten objects; and the pure also has ten objects.
That attained in the desire realm, regarding the <s>dharmas</s> and meanings of the upper realms, has three in its own ground regarding consciousness;
those attained in the form realm, to be abandoned by meditation, are universals and underlie.

children.text: catvāraḥ parivṛtte sve rūpāptāḥ khalvapi trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Four are in one's own transformed realm; those attained in the form realm are indeed also three.
Those belonging to the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), together with the universal ones, are eliminated by the path of <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation). // Abhidh-d_333 //
Likewise in the second [truth] and in the fifth [category] as well,
those having <s>sāsrava</s> (defiled) objects <s>anuśerate</s> (lie latent) in their own [realm] and in the third [truth] also. // Abhidh-d_334 //
But when reversed, those obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) that have <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) objects as their support,
the rest should be stated as before; in the fourth [truth] also, as in the third. // Abhidh-d_335 //
But when reversed, those obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> — the four — elsewhere as before,

children.text: rūpāpte prathame 'dhastāt trayaḥ sve khalvapi trayaḥ // Abhidh-d_336 //
children.translated_text: those obtained in <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm): in the first [truth], three from below, and in one's own [realm] indeed also three. // Abhidh-d_336 //
Those of the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), the universal ones, together with those eliminated by the path of <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation),
when reversed, three from below and four from one's own <s>dhātu</s> (realm). // Abhidh-d_337 //
And four <s>nikāyas</s> (classes) obtained in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm) lie latent.

children.text: tadvadeva dvitīye 'pi pañcame 'pi tathaiva ca // Abhidh-d_338 //
children.translated_text: Likewise in the second [truth] and in the fifth [category] as well. // Abhidh-d_338 //
Those having <s>sāsrava</s> (defiled) objects lie latent in their own [realm] and in the third [truth] also.
But when reversed, those obtained in <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) that have <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) objects as their support. // Abhidh-d_339 //
The rest should be known as before; in the fourth [truth] also, as in the third.
When reversed, in the first [stage] of <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), one should understand as in the third. // Abhidh-d_340 //
In one's own [realm], three; those obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) and those obtained in <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) — three and three respectively.
When reversed, as for those obtained in <s>rūpadhātu</s>, in the second and fifth likewise. // Abhidh-d_341 //
In the third [truth] indeed, and in one's own [realm], those having <s>sāsrava</s> (defiled) objects as their support.
When reversed, those obtained in one's own <s>dhātu</s> (realm) that have <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) objects as their support. // Abhidh-d_342 //
The rest should be stated as in the first; in the fourth [truth] also, as in the third.

children.text: ādyavattu parāvṛtte vijñāne nirdiśed budhaḥ // Abhidh-d_343 //
children.translated_text: But when reversed, the wise one should teach regarding <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as in the first. // Abhidh-d_343 //
The <s>nikāya</s> (class) to be abandoned by the path of <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation), together with the universal ones,
lies latent, obtained in two <s>dhātus</s> (realms), and those of the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm) [lie latent] in the <s>cakṣurindriya</s> (eye faculty). // Abhidh-d_344 //
The <s>nikāyas</s> (classes) obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) and <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), in the domain of the <s>cakṣurindriya</s> (eye faculty),
those to be abandoned by the seeing of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>hetu</s> (origin), <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view), and <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) — three and three. // Abhidh-d_345 //
Those of the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), to be abandoned by <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation), and the universal ones, lie latent.
But when reversed, four — excluding those eliminated by the seeing of <s>samyakdṛṣṭi</s> (right view). // Abhidh-d_346 //

children.text: duḥkhendriye tu kāmāptaḥ svaireva saha sarvagaiḥ /
children.translated_text: But regarding the <s>duḥkhendriya</s> (pain faculty), that obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), together with its own universal ones only.

children.text: tadgocare tu vijñāne nikāyā anuśerate // Abhidh-d_347 //
children.translated_text: But in the domain of that, in <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), the <s>nikāyas</s> (classes) lie latent. // Abhidh-d_347 //
Three obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), those of <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), together with the universal ones and those eliminated by <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice).

children.text: paravṛtte tu catvāraḥ kāmāptā anuśerate // Abhidh-d_348 //
children.translated_text: But when reversed, four obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) lie latent. // Abhidh-d_348 //
Three from the last of <s>rūpabhava</s> (form existence), the universal ones to be abandoned by <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation),
all four lie latent when reversed in two [ways]. // Abhidh-d_349 //
Regarding the <s>sukhendriya</s> (pleasure faculty), its object, <s>citta</s> (mind), and its domain also,
those obtained from <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) onward, according to connection, and the universal ones lie latent. // Abhidh-d_350 //
But those comprised in the three <s>dhātus</s> (realms), all [lie latent] in the <s>manasindriya</s> (mental faculty),
in the <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) that has that as its object, having all <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) things as its domain. // Abhidh-d_351 //
Only those having <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned) objects lie latent when reversed.

children.text: viśeṣo dviḥparāvṛttau vidyate 'tra na kaścana // Abhidh-d_352 //
children.translated_text: In the double reversal, there is no distinction whatsoever here. // Abhidh-d_352 //
From the <s>citta</s> (mind) that is to be abandoned by the seeing of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) onward, the <s>cittas</s> (minds) of one in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm)

children.text: bhavatyanantaraṃ ṣaḍ vā tasyorddhvaṃ pañca pañca vā // Abhidh-d_353 //
children.translated_text: become immediately [following] — either six, or above that, five or five. // Abhidh-d_353 //
But for one born in <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), one should specify the <s>cittas</s> (minds):

children.text: ekaṃ vā pañca vā ṣaḍ vā sapta vā yadi vā daśa // Abhidh-d_354 //
children.translated_text: either one, or five, or six, or seven, or ten. // Abhidh-d_354 //
For one born in <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), one should determine these <s>cittas</s> (minds):
those of one's own <s>dhātu</s> (realm) — five only; at the time of death, ten from elsewhere. // Abhidh-d_355 //
<s>Citta</s> (mind) is considered to be 'with <s>anuśaya</s> (latent defilement)' in two ways: by accompaniment and by the state of lying latent.
Or in two ways — defiled and undefiled — it is designated as one single [category]. // Abhidh-d_356 //
From <s>moha</s> (delusion) arises <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body), from that <s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view),
from that <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt), from that <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view), from that view <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (attachment to rules and rituals). // Abhidh-d_357 //
<s>Rāga</s> (attachment) [arises] regarding one's own view, <s>māna</s> (pride) as well, and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) is manifested elsewhere.
This sequence of these [defilements] should be known from the predominance of their occurrence. // Abhidh-d_358 //
But due to association with good, bad, and neutral [companions], the irregularity of their occurrence is acknowledged.
A certain <s>kleśa</s> (defilement) arises when the three causes are complete. // Abhidh-d_359 //

children.text: vyavidyāḥ sakalāḥ kleśāḥ kāme kāmāsravo mataḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) except <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) are considered <s>kāmāsrava</s> (outflow of desire).
Excluding <s>styāna</s> (torpor) and <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), those above [in the higher realms] are <s>bhavāsrava</s> (outflow of existence), due to their similarity. // Abhidh-d_360 //
But that called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), being the root, is <s>avidyāsrava</s> (outflow of ignorance) pertaining to all <s>dhātus</s> (realms).
Likewise the <s>oghas</s> (floods) and <s>yogas</s> (bonds) — excluding <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (views), their separate [classification] is due to their strength. // Abhidh-d_361 //

children.text: sāvidyā dve upādāne yathāktau dve tu dṛṅmaye /
children.translated_text: Together with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), two <s>upādānas</s> (clinging) as stated; but two are made of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (views).
The four also [have] one final single one, based on wrong path and so forth. // Abhidh-d_362 //
The rest belong to the three <s>dhātus</s> (realms), and in the final, due to the functioning of <s>ātmabhāva</s> (self-existence).
Through the terms <s>saṃyojana</s> (fetters) and so forth, they are shown again in five ways. // Abhidh-d_363 //
In this [system] there are nine <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters), and <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy) and <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) as well.
Due to the commonality of the substance of <s>amarṣaṇa</s> (intolerance), two fetters of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (views). // Abhidh-d_364 //
The remaining five <s>anuśayas</s> (latent defilements), again in five ways each.
He taught the <s>avarabhāgīya</s> (lower fetters) and the <s>ūrdhvabhāgīya</s> (upper fetters). // Abhidh-d_365 //

children.text: ādyantye dve dṛśau kāṅkṣākāmacchando dvireva yaḥ /
children.translated_text: The first and last two <s>dṛṣṭis</s> (views), <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt), and <s>kāmacchanda</s> (desire for sensual pleasures) which is twofold,
by two [one achieves] non-return to <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), and by three the bringing back [is prevented]. // Abhidh-d_366 //
Because the function of what is to be abandoned by two and one views is stated, and because of the inclusion of what is to be abandoned by seeing,
even though all are to be abandoned by seeing, these three are proclaimed [separately]. // Abhidh-d_367 //
Because [<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>] is the cause of all misfortune, because it is antagonistic to the <s>mārga</s> (path),
and because it is devoid of true comprehension — [thus is] the teaching of the three <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters). // Abhidh-d_368 //

Two <s>rāgas</s> (attachments) born of <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) and <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), and three — <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>moha</s> (delusion), and <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness).
Because of lying latent with three <s>vedanās</s> (feelings) and because of firmness — three <s>bandhanas</s> (bonds). // Abhidh-d_369 //
Because of binding both sides, four <s>granthas</s> (knots) are proclaimed:
that called <s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness), likewise <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and the two [types of] <s>parāmarśa</s> (clinging). // Abhidh-d_370 //
The <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions) should be known as <s>saṃrambha</s> (fury) and so forth, as stated.

children.text: sarve vā caitasāḥ kliṣṭāḥ saṃskāraskandhasaṃjñitāḥ // Abhidh-d_371 //
children.translated_text: Or all defiled <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors) designated as <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations). // Abhidh-d_371 //
But those other than the root <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) and <s>malas</s> (impurities) are designated as six <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions):
<s>śāṭhya</s> (deceit), <s>upanāha</s> (enmity), <s>pradāśa</s> (spite), <s>māyā</s> (fraud), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), and <s>viheṭhanā</s> (malice). // Abhidh-d_372 //

<s>Mrakṣa</s> (concealment), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness), <s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>middha</s> (drowsiness), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), <s>krodha</s> (anger),

children.text: mātsaryaṃ kukṛtatvaṃ ca daśadhā paryavasthitiḥ // Abhidh-d_373 //
children.translated_text: <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness), and <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) — the <s>paryavasthānas</s> (entanglements) are tenfold. // Abhidh-d_373 //
From these, <s>ānunaya</s> (complacency) and its outflow — <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), and so forth —
<s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment), <s>anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness), <s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>middha</s> (drowsiness) and so forth arise from <s>moha</s> (delusion). // Abhidh-d_374 //
<s>Kaukṛtya</s> (regret) arises from <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt); <s>krodha</s> (anger) and so forth arise from <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion).
<s>Pramāda</s> (heedlessness), <s>stambha</s> (rigidity), <s>mārdava</s> (?), <s>māyā</s> (fraud), <s>śāṭhya</s> (deceit), and <s>vijṛmbhikā</s> (yawning). // Abhidh-d_375 //
<s>Kāyadauṣṭhulya</s> (physical heaviness) and so forth should be known as arising from mixed [causes].
<s>Pradāśa</s> (spite) is the outflow of <s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s> (clinging to views); <s>śaṭhatā</s> (dishonesty) [is the outflow] of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (views). // Abhidh-d_376 //
The conjunction of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) and with <s>sukha</s> (physical pleasure),

children.text: dveṣasya daurmanasyena duḥkhena ca nigadyate // Abhidh-d_377 //
children.translated_text: and that of <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) with <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure) and with <s>duḥkha</s> (physical pain) is declared. // Abhidh-d_377 //
Of <s>moha</s> (delusion) with all [five] <s>vedanās</s> (feelings), both <s>caitasī</s> (mental); unlike <s>asaddṛṣṭi</s> (wrong views),

children.text: kāṅkṣā ca daurmanasyena śeṣāṇāṃ sumanastayā // Abhidh-d_378 //
children.translated_text: <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt) also [is associated] with <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure); the rest with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure). // Abhidh-d_378 //
But with <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), all — this is the rule for those obtained in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm).
For those born in other <s>dhātus</s> (realms), [the association is] with their own [feelings], differing by each level. // Abhidh-d_379 //
<s>Īrṣyā</s> (envy) [is associated] with <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure), likewise <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) and <s>krodha</s> (anger),
and <s>pradāśa</s> (spite), <s>upanāha</s> (enmity), and <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harm) likewise. // Abhidh-d_380 //
<s>Mātsarya</s> (miserliness) [is associated] with <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure); for some, with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure).

children.text: dvābhyāṃ māyā tathā śāṭhyaṃ mrakṣo middhaṃ tathaiva ca // Abhidh-d_381 //
children.translated_text: With both — <s>māyā</s> (fraud), likewise <s>śāṭhya</s> (deceit), <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment), and <s>middha</s> (drowsiness) as well. // Abhidh-d_381 //
But <s>mada</s> (intoxication) is conjoined with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) and <s>sukha</s> (physical pleasure).
<s>Āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness), <s>styāna</s> (torpor), and <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness) with five [feelings]. // Abhidh-d_382 //
One should know those by means of the last [truth] that has a combined object, through [the aspects of] impermanence and so forth.
The complete destruction of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) [is achieved] by the last [truth], or by one with an undifferentiated object. // Abhidh-d_384 //
These three, having undifferentiated objects, are taught in two ways.
For one thus seeing, the direct perception of arising and passing away // Abhidh-d_385 //
arises subsequently regarding the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), like a potter's wheel and so forth.
He examines the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). // Abhidh-d_386 //
Having applied that to the [four] <s>satyas</s> (truths), then someone examines [further].
Having ascertained their <s>anityatva</s> (impermanence) and <s>duḥkhatva</s> (suffering-nature), then again, // Abhidh-d_387 //
seeing [them as] without an agent, without purposeful activity, and arising dependent on conditions,
he cultivates the <s>tattvākāra</s> (aspect of reality) that in all [dharmas] there is no <s>ātman</s> (self). // Abhidh-d_388 //
For one who sees the absence of a controller and the state of being dependent [on others],

children.text: sarvadharmeṣu nairātmye sthirā buddhiḥ pravartate // Abhidh-d_389 //
children.translated_text: a firm <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) regarding <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) in all <s>dharmas</s> arises. // Abhidh-d_389 //
Because [they are] not empty of their own nature, the <s>dharmamudrās</s> (seals of dharma) are proclaimed.

children.text: taduktyā ca taduktatvācchūnyākāro na deśitaḥ // Abhidh-d_390 //
children.translated_text: And because that is stated by that statement, the <s>śūnyākāra</s> (aspect of emptiness) is not taught [separately]. // Abhidh-d_390 //
Through the doors of <s>gotra</s> (lineage), groups, and so forth, of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and so forth, as appropriate,
one constantly examines through the two marks — specific and general. // Abhidh-d_391 //
Then, for each <s>skandha</s> (aggregate), regarding their intrinsic nature and so forth, truly,
there arises progressively skill in the seven stations. // Abhidh-d_392 //
For one who progressively churns the fire-stick of <s>duḥkhasatya</s> (truth of suffering),
who has <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and <s>vīrya</s> (effort) as companions, seeking the fire of true knowledge, // Abhidh-d_393 //
then knowledge that has fallen upon the [sixteen] aspects, which determines pacification,
born of <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), called <s>ūṣman</s> (heat), arises along with its accompaniments. // Abhidh-d_394 //
Then likewise the <s>mūrdhānas</s> (summits), which destroy <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong views),
having greater power than the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat) [stage], increasing faith in the [three] <s>ratnas</s> (jewels). // Abhidh-d_395 //

body.translated_text: ........ and in this, the last in both cases. // Abhidh-d_396 //

children.translated_text: One meditates on the seeing of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth at first, not on one who sees <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
One should teach aspects of similar kind everywhere here. // Abhidh-d_397 //
One should see any one of those [four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>] as presently arisen in the stage of increase,
any one of the four as presently arisen in the stage of increase. // Abhidh-d_398 //
But future ones are meditated upon — certainly all four here.
In the final [stage] of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), those that have come face to face — all the future ones indeed are complete. // Abhidh-d_399 //
Indeed all the aspects are meditated upon from the attainment of <s>gotra</s> (lineage).
But at the attainment of <s>gotra</s> (lineage), one should know the meditation on similar aspects. // Abhidh-d_400 //
In the spreading [stage] of <s>mūrdhānas</s> (summits) everywhere, in the increase of the spreading of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation),
those called <s>dharmā</s> [<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>] that have come face to face — four, indeed future. // Abhidh-d_401 //
All the aspects there are meditated upon from the attainment of <s>gotra</s> (lineage).
From all [<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>], any one arisen, in the increase of three truths. // Abhidh-d_402 //
And four future ones are certainly meditated upon there.

children.text: ākārāḥ sakalā jñeyāḥ kṣāntivinyasane śṛṇu // Abhidh-d_403 //
children.translated_text: All the aspects should be known — listen regarding the arrangement of <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance). // Abhidh-d_403 //
Everywhere the last ones have arisen; four are indeed future.
All the aspects there are meditated upon, and also the future ones. // Abhidh-d_404 //
In the <s>agradharmas</s> (supreme dharmas), the presently [arisen] <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness) is called <s>dharmā</s> (of dharmas).
But future ones are meditated upon — certainly four in these. // Abhidh-d_405 //
Indeed four aspects, due to similarity with the <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing).
As in the spreading of <s>ūṣman</s> (heat), so should it be seen on the path of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (seeing). // Abhidh-d_406 //
One should specify the last one as presently [arisen] in the <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge of the path).
Four future ones likewise — meditations on the sixteen aspects. // Abhidh-d_407 //
And beyond that, for the <s>ārya</s> (noble one), at the arising of all previously unattained qualities,

children.text: śrutacintāmayaṃ hitvā sūkṣmasūkṣmaṃ vyapohya ca // Abhidh-d_408 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned that born of <s>śruta</s> (learning) and <s>cintā</s> (reflection), and having removed the progressively subtler [defilements], // Abhidh-d_408 //
but for the beginner on the path of practice, through the conquering of four <s>bhūmis</s> (levels),
any one of those that has arisen, and four indeed future. // Abhidh-d_409 //
On the <s>ānantaryamārga</s> (uninterrupted path), freed; in the last, all future ones.
In the last <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), in the eight paths beginning with the preparatory, as before. // Abhidh-d_410 //
But one should know three in the ninth, from entry into the fundamental level.
But in the preparatory [stage] of the <s>sāmantaka</s> (preliminary meditation), four, or the last may be. // Abhidh-d_411 //
In the <s>divyacakṣus</s> (divine eye), <s>divyaśrotra</s> (divine ear), <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge), in the <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation) and so forth likewise,
the first one that has come face to face — four are indeed future. // Abhidh-d_412 //
But in <s>paracittajñāna</s> (knowledge of others' minds), the third, and four also future.
In <s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s> (recollection of past lives) and the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), the last — all future. // Abhidh-d_413 //
Regarding the <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) of the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm), one should state any one of three.

children.text: saṃmukhe nāma jātāstu tisra eva vinirdiśet // Abhidh-d_414 //
children.translated_text: Those arisen face to face — one should specify exactly three. // Abhidh-d_414 //
But in the <s>ārūpya</s> (formless) and <s>kṛtsna</s> (totality) [meditations], one should declare the last as presently arisen.
Three that have not [yet] arisen — one states with certainty. // Abhidh-d_415 //

children.text: āryasya khalu vairāgyaprayoge kṣepaṇe pi ca /
children.translated_text: For the <s>ārya</s> (noble one), indeed, in the practice of <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment) and in the casting off also,
From all [the foundations of mindfulness], one arises that has not yet occurred, and four are future. // Abhidh-d_416 //
On the <s>ānantaryamārga</s> (uninterrupted path), the last ones are liberated; but all [remaining ones] are future.

children.text: ṛdhyādau tu guṇāḥ sarvamanāryasyaiva nirdiśet // Abhidh-d_417 //
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural powers) and so forth, all qualities should be taught only for the non-noble person. // Abhidh-d_417 //
Regarding the last [and] first [stages], the recollection of past lives and so forth, the <s>dharma-pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of dharmas),
likewise regarding the subsequent <s>samādhis</s> and so forth, and regarding the <s>āvaraṇā</s> (obstruction) as well, // Abhidh-d_418 //
regarding the <s>vimokṣas</s> called <s>ārūpya</s> (formless) and so forth, and likewise at the arising of the subtle <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception),
from all [the foundations], one arises that has not yet occurred, and indeed four are future. // Abhidh-d_419 //
But regarding the subtlest of the subtle, one should state that the last one has occurred and three are future.
In brief, this has been declared as the cultivation of <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness). // Abhidh-d_420 //
This <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) [practice] is fourfold, produced by cultivation,
having six planes, sixteen aspects, and [consisting of] five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) excluding <s>āpti</s> (acquisition). // Abhidh-d_421 //
Afterwards, however, comes the penetration (<s>nirvedha</s>), which is then called the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>);
since it is a definite penetration, it is called <s>nirvedha</s> (penetration). // Abhidh-d_422 //
The inclination of <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas) toward suffering [produces] the pure <s>dharmadarśana</s> (seeing of dharmas);
then, regarding that very [truth], the ascertainment—<s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas) follows immediately. // Abhidh-d_423 //
Likewise with respect to the three [remaining] truths, the <s>anvayadhī</s> (inferential cognition) is twofold in each case.
The moments of the <s>dṛṅmārga</s> (path of seeing) there should be known as having fifteen characteristics. // Abhidh-d_424 //

body.translated_text: The last moment belongs to the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of cultivation); this is a fruit, established by the accomplishment of the goal. // Abhidh-d_425 //

children.translated_text: One [type of <s>anāgāmin</s>] passes through the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) sequentially; the fifth, however, goes to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>;
another goes to the formless realm in four ways; yet another attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the visible [life]. // Abhidh-d_426 //

children.text: punastridhā tridhā kṛtvā trīnato rūpagā nava /
children.translated_text: Again, dividing threefold into three, from these [arise] nine who are reborn in the form realm.
The distinction among these should further be known through the division of <s>karma</s> (action), <s>kleśa</s> (defilements), and faculties (<s>akṣa</s>). // Abhidh-d_427 //
Together with the six who are <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> (stream-upward), the good destiny (<s>sadgati</s>) is considered sevenfold.
Due to the irreversibility of their conduct, the good destiny is declared only for these. // Abhidh-d_428 //
For the noble one whose rebirth-existence is turned back does not go to another realm here;
and this upward course [is maintained], and one who is an <s>arhat</s> does not suffer decline. // Abhidh-d_429 //
The last one in <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) first proceeds; the attainment is due to the combination of two moments.

children.text: udbhavārthaṃ sukhārthaṃ ca kleśāśaṅkārthameva ca // Abhidh-d_430 //
children.translated_text: For the purpose of arising, for the purpose of happiness, and for the very purpose of [allaying] fear of defilements, // Abhidh-d_430 //
because of the fivefold [nature] of that, the five <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (pure abodes) are remembered;

children.text: na jātu dṛṣṭapūrvāstāḥ sarvairapi pṛthagjanaiḥ // Abhidh-d_431 //
children.translated_text: these have never been seen before by any <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person). // Abhidh-d_431 //
One who attains <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment) is a <s>kāyasākṣin</s> (body-witness);
up to the abandoner of the eight parts of <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence), one is a practitioner progressing toward <s>arhatship</s>. // Abhidh-d_432 //
And one who abides on the last <s>ānantaryamārga</s> (uninterrupted path), called <s>vajropama</s> (diamond-like),

children.text: tatphalārthaṃ kṣayajñānaṃ tadekālambanaṃ na vā // Abhidh-d_433 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction) [arises] for the fruit of that—whether it has the same object or not. // Abhidh-d_433 //
Upon attaining that, one is an <s>aśaikṣa</s> (one beyond training), an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one), honored by the three worlds,
completely disjoined from all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), having gone beyond the three trainings (<s>śikṣātraya</s>). // Abhidh-d_434 //
The path called <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation) is twofold, by the distinction of impure and pure.
But the one called <s>darśana</s> (seeing) should be known as entirely <s>nirāsrava</s> (undefiled) in all cases. // Abhidh-d_435 //
In sequential [practice], since the greater part [consists of] those with and without detachment, [and those] between the detached and non-detached,
the [path] called <s>aśaikṣa</s> (beyond training) should also be understood as always immaculate. // Abhidh-d_436 //

body.translated_text: The pure one transcends <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence)........ // Abhidh-d_437 //

children.translated_text: Since, having abandoned the distinguished [defilements], one attains the supreme fruit,
the <s>śaikṣa</s> (trainee) [has it] through three [factors] beginning with guarding the faculties, and the <s>arhat</s> has it complete through two. // Abhidh-d_438 //
In brief, the path should be understood as fourfold again:
called <s>ānantarya</s> (uninterrupted) and <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), characterized by commencement and excellence. // Abhidh-d_439 //
For one of sharp faculties, the practice in the fundamental <s>dhyānas</s> is pleasant;
for one of dull intellect, [the attainment of] <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges) is slow; the opposite for the other, due to reversal. // Abhidh-d_440 //
<s>Kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction) is considered <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), and so also is <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising);

children.text: daśa caikaśca tatpakṣyāḥ saptatriṃśattu nāmataḥ // Abhidh-d_441 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>bodhipakṣya</s> (factors conducive to awakening) are ten and one, but thirty-seven by name. // Abhidh-d_441 //
With <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>prīti</s> (joy), and <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention), and the five faculties beginning with <s>śraddhā</s> (faith),
with <s>prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility)—[these are] produced from two [categories of] form; but the distinction in name is due to [different] perspectives. // Abhidh-d_442 //
The <s>balas</s> (powers) are none other than the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties); <s>smṛtyupasthiti</s> (foundation of mindfulness) is simply <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).
<s>Vīrya</s> (energy) is called <s>samyakpradhāna</s> (right exertion); the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power) are mental stability (<s>manasthiti</s>). // Abhidh-d_443 //
The elimination of faults, [their] non-arising, the production of qualities, [and their] increase—
that which accomplishes each of these at once, that indeed is the fourfold <s>prahāṇa</s> (exertion). // Abhidh-d_444 //
<s>Chanda</s> (desire), <s>vyāyāma</s> (effort), <s>mīmāṃsā</s> (investigation), and <s>citta</s> (mind)—drawn [by these], the <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations)
are the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the sources of the attainment of qualities. // Abhidh-d_445 //
The fivefold group beginning with <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is declared as faculties (<s>indriya</s>) because of sovereignty over the three [aspects of] awakening;
the same is designated by the word <s>bala</s> (power) because of not being overpowered [by opposing forces]. // Abhidh-d_446 //
The sevenfold <s>bodhyaṅga</s> (factors of awakening) was taught by the Teacher for the purpose of awakening;
with reference to the ultimate, [the last factor] is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)—to the very end, through [its] assistance. // Abhidh-d_447 //
Of <s>prīti</s> (joy), <s>prasrabdhi</s> (tranquility), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), the status as limbs [of awakening] is stated because of being causes;
of the group of four beginning with <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention), [they are limbs] of the path, due to being conducive to what is to be known. // Abhidh-d_448 //
Having knowledge as its light, the plane of refined discernment, accompanied by moral conduct, with mindfulness and energy as friends,
enjoying the supreme bliss of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) over all—this path leads to the abode of the twofold liberation. // Abhidh-d_449 //
The predominance of the seven groups [of <s>bodhipakṣya</s> dharmas] in the stages beginning with <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat)
should be understood in sequence with respect to the <s>bhāvanā</s> (cultivation) and <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (seeing) paths. // Abhidh-d_450 //
<s>Citta</s> (mind) is not [counted as a <s>bodhipakṣya</s>] because it is king-like, because it follows both qualities and faults;
because it conforms to conventional usage, <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) is not accepted among these. // Abhidh-d_451 //
<s>Cetanā</s> (volition) is not [included] because it inclines toward the fruit of <s>vipāka</s> (maturation), and because the path is [already] stated;
<s>manaskāra</s> (attention) is not [included] because of non-predominance, since it operates in both knowledge and ignorance. // Abhidh-d_452 //
<s>Chanda</s> (desire) is not [included] because of the predominance of initiating action, since it strengthens <s>vīrya</s> (energy);
<s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve) is not because of [the tendency toward] superimposition; <s>sparśa</s> (contact) is not because of the difficulty of discerning [it]. // Abhidh-d_453 //
<s>Hrī</s> (shame) and <s>apatrāpya</s> (moral dread) are not <s>āryavaṃśa</s> (noble lineage), because they function without [full] confidence;
<s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness) is not because of being other-directed; <s>avihiṃsā</s> (non-harming) is not because of [merely] not hurting. // Abhidh-d_454 //
<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), and the rest are not [included] because they operate with beings as their basis;
the <s>avetyaprasādas</s> (confirmed confidences) are also not, because of being only a part of the path-limbs and faculties. // Abhidh-d_455 //
<s>Adveṣa</s> (non-hatred) is not [included separately] from the <s>kuśalamūlas</s> (wholesome roots) because of having beings as its object;
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not because of indifference; [external] sound is not because of its remoteness. // Abhidh-d_456 //
The <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) are free from impurity because of being nearest to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening);
the others are [also] conducive to awakening—both impure and pure. // Abhidh-d_457 //
In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, all [<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>] are [present]; in the fundamental <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary meditation), <s>prīti</s> (joy) is excluded;
in the second [<s>dhyāna</s>] also, <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention) is excluded; and in the two [higher <s>dhyānas</s>], both of these [are absent]. // Abhidh-d_458 //
From the <s>śīla</s> (morality) limbs and from those two, [the limbs] should be seen in the three formless [attainments];
from all the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, in the desire realm, the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> are excluded. // Abhidh-d_459 //
Those four primacies that are declared there by the learned:
in entering the <s>nyāma</s> (certainty), detachment, attainment of fruits, and increase of faculties. // Abhidh-d_460 //
Of the eight undefiled path-limbs, in their respective [positions],
for each of these, in the [three] time-periods, the gain and non-gain should be known through nine bases. // Abhidh-d_461 //
The gain [occurs] in the realization of the three truths regarding moral conduct and the <s>dharmaprasāda</s> (confidence in the Dharma);
in the seeing of the truth of the path, also regarding <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> as objects [of confidence]. // Abhidh-d_462 //
The faith regarding truth, apart from that of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Saṅgha</s>, and the path,
that <s>avetyaprasāda</s> (confirmed confidence) in the <s>Dharma</s>, because it does not arise from intimate conviction [alone]. // Abhidh-d_463 //
One who is a <s>Buddha</s> by [virtue of] the destruction of delusion, sleep, and darkness, by the opening of the eye of wisdom by oneself—

children.text: buddho yastadguṇe śraddhā prasādaḥ sa jine mataḥ // Abhidh-d_464 //
children.translated_text: faith in his qualities is the <s>prasāda</s> (confidence) in the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), it is held. // Abhidh-d_464 //
That which is the mine of <s>pudgalas</s> (persons) endowed with the qualities of the <s>śaikṣa</s> (trainees) and <s>aśaikṣa</s> (those beyond training),
faith having their qualities as object is the <s>prasāda</s> (confidence) regarding the <s>Saṅgha</s>. // Abhidh-d_465 //
The purity of moral precepts (<s>śīla</s>)—that is likewise a <s>prasāda</s> (confirmed confidence);
in substance these are only two, but by name they are a group of four. // Abhidh-d_466 //
Because the <s>śaikṣa</s> (trainee) still has remaining bonds, <s>vimukti</s> (liberation) is not accepted as a limb [for them];
because it has the nature of release and confirmed release, it is twofold as impermanent and permanent. // Abhidh-d_467 //

children.text: pūrvoktaiva hi yā bodhiḥ sā samyagjñānamucyate /
children.translated_text: That which was previously stated as <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is called <s>samyagjñāna</s> (right knowledge);
the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (one beyond training) mind is freed from future [defilements] through the obstruction of <s>kleśas</s>. // Abhidh-d_468 //
In the world, one engaged in dharmic activity is also considered as engaged in <s>dharma</s>;
but the path, having undertaken [right] conduct, dispels that covering. // Abhidh-d_469 //
That <s>vimukti</s> (liberation) which is eternal—those three are <s>virāga</s> (dispassion) and so forth;

children.text: ākhyātā dhātavaḥ sūtre tridhā bhedo hyapekṣayā // Abhidh-d_470 //
children.translated_text: they are declared as <s>dhātus</s> (elements) in the <s>sūtra</s>; the threefold division is indeed with reference [to different aspects]. // Abhidh-d_470 //
<s>Virāga</s> (dispassion) is the release from <s>rāga</s> (attachment); that called <s>prahāṇa</s> (abandonment) is the destruction of others;
<s>nirodhadhātu</s> (element of cessation) is the cessation of the remaining conditioned things. // Abhidh-d_471 //
The <s>yogin</s> becomes disenchanted through cognition that depends on suffering and its cause;
one who was attached becomes detached—hence the fourfold culmination. // Abhidh-d_472 //
The <s>saṃjñās</s> (perceptions) beginning with <s>anityasaṃjñā</s> (perception of impermanence) are ten; from these [arise the perceptions] beginning with <s>aśubha</s> (the impure);
three [comprise] the mode of the path and the path [itself]; four are the final [group]; three are the fruit. // Abhidh-d_473 //
The triad beginning with <s>aśubhasaṃjñā</s> (perception of impurity) and so forth should be known as <s>sāsrava</s> (defiled);

children.text: samalā nirmalāstvanyā bodhyā nava bhuvo 'malāḥ // Abhidh-d_474 //
children.translated_text: impure [and] pure are the others; nine planes [have them as] pure, to be awakened to. // Abhidh-d_474 //
Among the eleven planes, the last [perception] should be identified in [the stages beginning with] the <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth;

children.text: caturthī pañcamī ṣaṣṭhī vidyāt saptasu bhūmiṣu // Abhidh-d_475 //
children.translated_text: the fourth, fifth, and sixth should be known in seven planes. // Abhidh-d_475 //
This world, deluded about the true nature of things, is confused regarding the knowable reality;
I shall expound those <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges) with elaboration of their own nature and so forth. // Abhidh-d_476 //
Having set aside species and substance, with reference to the antidote and so forth,
its division is proclaimed as tenfold, with names [beginning with] <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas). // Abhidh-d_477 //
Two [knowledges are distinguished] by the objects <s>dharma</s> (direct) and <s>anvaya</s> (inferential); a group of four by suffering and so forth;
two by <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional) and knowledge of others' minds; two by <s>kṣaya</s> (destruction) and <s>anutpāda</s> (non-arising). // Abhidh-d_478 //
Through antidote and application, through own-nature, aspect, and object—
their establishment should be understood; or by function and by accumulation. // Abhidh-d_479 //
Regarding <s>dhātus</s> (realms), truths, objects, and minds, regarding birth, cessation, and non-arising—

children.text: saṃmohasya nivṛttyarthaṃ tadbhedo daśadhaiva vā // Abhidh-d_480 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of removing delusion, their division is indeed tenfold. // Abhidh-d_480 //

body.translated_text: The understanding that [suffering] is fully known and so forth—<s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction) regarding suffering and the rest is the fruit. // Abhidh-d_481 //
Cognition has aspects; it always operates with aspects; [cognitions] with aspects are dependent [on objects]. // Abhidh-d_482 //

children.translated_text: Knowledge of others' minds [comprises] three [aspects]; <s>nirodhadhī</s> (cognition of cessation) is designated as <s>dharmasaṃjñā</s> (having dharma-designation);
the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) are from this—the remaining knowledge is accepted. // Abhidh-d_483 //

body.translated_text: The objects of cognition are ninefold, [falling within] the domain of <s>mārga</s> (path), <s>dharma</s> (direct), and <s>anvaya</s> (inferential) knowledges. // Abhidh-d_484 //

children.translated_text: Having divided the five dharmas obtained across three realms, which have the nature of the path, [and are] eternal,
into two, for the purpose of analysis, one should show the domain of knowledge. // Abhidh-d_485 //
On the <s>dṛṅmārga</s> (path of seeing), at the first knowledge, one is endowed with three knowledges;
with one increase in each of the four [subsequent moments], the detached one [proceeds] upward with knowledge of others' minds. // Abhidh-d_486 //
In detachment from desire through three <s>dhyānas</s>, at the last path of liberation,
and in the application of the fundamental <s>dhyānas</s>, the cultivation of future [knowledge] should be known. // Abhidh-d_487 //
For the ordinary person, in the arising of <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and so forth,
on the paths of application and liberation, <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional) and knowledge of others' minds [are operative]. // Abhidh-d_488 //
<s>Kṣāntis</s> (patient acceptances) and <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges) of the same type are cultivated on the <s>dṛkpatha</s> (path of seeing);
conventional [knowledge] also [is cultivated] in the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge) designated as suffering and cause. // Abhidh-d_489 //
Because of having the same antidote, because of being of the nature of path among these,
therefore, the <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization) is so called, because of the attainment at the end of the three truths. // Abhidh-d_490 //

children.text: mārgākhye tvanvayajñāne ṣaḍ bhāvyante 'tha sapta vā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge) called 'of the path,' six or seven are cultivated;
and on the <s>ānantaryamārga</s> (uninterrupted path) above, knowledge of others' minds is not cultivated. // Abhidh-d_491 //
On the paths of abandonment and liberation, except from the liberation of the last [stage],
because of being the antidote to <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence), conventional [knowledge] is not cultivated. // Abhidh-d_492 //
That which, regarding the own-nature and so forth of the <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth, extends without obstruction—
that, designated as the knowledge of <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth, is the power (<s>bala</s>) consisting of nine knowledges. // Abhidh-d_493 //
That which operates in discerning the softness and so forth of the faculties of beings—
that is the power of knowledge of the supreme and inferior faculties, consisting of nine cognitions. // Abhidh-d_494 //
That which operates regarding the varied inclinations of beings, whether inferior and so forth, in three [categories]—
that power, designated as knowledge of various inclinations, also consists of nine [cognitions]. // Abhidh-d_495 //
That which, called knowledge regarding various <s>dhātus</s> (elements), operates for the benefit of beings—
that power of knowledge of various elements, like [the previous], consists of nine knowledges. // Abhidh-d_496 //
That which knows the distinction of destinies, dharmas, and noble ones through the distinction of conditions—
those ten cognitions [constitute] the power of knowledge of the path leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminīpratipad</s>). // Abhidh-d_497 //
That which is designated as <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge), seeing one's own and others' past births—
that is the power of knowledge of recollection of former births (<s>prāgjātyanusmṛtijñāna</s>), together with its fruit, it is held. // Abhidh-d_498 //
That knowledge which operates in another time-period regarding the death and birth of beings—
that, called the cognition of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyutpattibuddhi</s>), is declared as a power, as stated before. // Abhidh-d_499 //
That which is designated as the knowledge of the destruction of <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) comprises six <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges), or alternatively ten;
the first of these has sixteen aspects, and the subsequent ones also [have aspects] by other [reckonings] according to [their] level. Abhidh-d_500
The seventh [power] has sixteen aspects, with two undifferentiated forms;

children.text: aṣṭākāraṃ dvitīyaṃ tu navajñānamayaṃ tu yat // Abhidh-d_501 //
children.translated_text: the second, however, has eight aspects, and consists of nine <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges). Abhidh-d_501
The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>bala</s> (power) is declared [thus]; it should be known as having twelve forms.
The first of these has all objects as its domain, while the last rests upon <s>śānti</s> (peace). Abhidh-d_502
The seventh has a twofold object comprising cause and existence, and has <s>satya</s> (truth) as its domain;
the eighth is said to have the past and other [times], elements, and objects [as its scope]. Abhidh-d_503
The ninth indeed has <s>rūpa</s> (form) as its object; the last apprehends the <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned).
This word '<s>bala</s>' (power) has a twofold reference; it is a power because of irresistibility. Abhidh-d_504

children.text: sandhau sandhau ca buddhasya kāyenārāyaṇaṃ balam /
children.translated_text: In every joint of the <s>Buddha</s>'s body there is the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
that [strength] is a <s>spraṣṭavya</s> (tangible), and it exceeds tenfold the [strength] of seven elephants and so forth. Abhidh-d_505
The fourfold <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness) [arises] from the attainment of the culmination of one's own and others' purposes.

children.text: ādyantabalarūpe dve dve karma pratipaddhiyoḥ // Abhidh-d_506 //
children.translated_text: The first and last are of the nature of <s>bala</s> (power); the [other] two pertain to <s>karma</s> (action) of the path and knowledge. Abhidh-d_506
The threefold <s>smṛtyupasthiti</s> (mindful establishment) depends on three [types of] listeners.
Its characteristic is <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension), with the capacity of mindful equipoise. Abhidh-d_507
Because it is of the nature of <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge), because of long-continued practice,
because of equal engagement everywhere and so forth, <s>mahākṛpā</s> (great compassion) belongs only to those who are bound [to saṃsāra for others' sake]. Abhidh-d_508
<s>Araṇā</s> (non-contention) and <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolution-knowledge) and the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges)

children.text: arhatsāntānikā hyete pañca tu prāntakoṭikāḥ // Abhidh-d_509 //
children.translated_text: belong to the <s>arhat</s>'s continuum; these five, however, pertain to the final limit. Abhidh-d_509
Qualities such as <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness) and others are shared with others as well.

children.text: eṣāṃ yathopadiṣṭānāṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam // Abhidh-d_510 //
children.translated_text: Hear now, I shall explain the characteristics of these as they have been taught. Abhidh-d_510
<s>Araṇā</s> (non-contention) is <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge), arising from dependence on the last <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) in the human [realm];
it belongs to the <s>ārya</s>'s (noble one's) continuum, is born [there], possesses a real basis, and is of a stainless nature. Abhidh-d_511
<s>Praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolution-knowledge) is likewise, but it apprehends all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena);
it is proclaimed as belonging to one with the <s>akopyadharma</s> (unshakeable quality); so too are the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges). Abhidh-d_512
They are distinguished by the non-confusion regarding the connection of intended meanings:
the first [<s>pratisaṃvid</s>] is [of meaning], the second manifests that [meaning], and should be known as investigating through knowledge. Abhidh-d_513
The third concerns verbal formations and destroys confusion regarding knowledge;
the fourth is continuous expression, oriented toward the production of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and so forth. Abhidh-d_514
That called <s>artha</s> (meaning) [analytical knowledge] pertains to all domains, comprising six <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges) or alternatively nine;
that called <s>pratibhāna</s> (ready speech) is likewise; but it consists of ten <s>jñānas</s>. Abhidh-d_515
In <s>kāma</s> (desire realm) and in the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) is the one called <s>dharma</s> [analytical knowledge]; the other [pertains to] the first [dhyāna] and <s>kāma</s> [realm].

children.text: saṃvṛtijñānamayyau tu dve ete pratisaṃvidau // Abhidh-d_516 //
children.translated_text: These two <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) consist of <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge). Abhidh-d_516

In <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power), in [divine] ear, in [knowledge of] others' minds, in [knowledge of] former [lives], in [knowledge of] death and rebirth, and in [knowledge of] the destruction [of outflows],
the <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) is the direct realization of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); there are six, or [it is] wisdom on the path of liberation. Abhidh-d_517
The [first] four are <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge); the mind-knowledge comprises five <s>jñānas</s>;
the <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) of the destruction of all <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) comprises six <s>jñānas</s>, or alternatively ten. Abhidh-d_518
The sixth [superknowledge] exists in all [realms]; the [other] five are in the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s> levels.
They are obtained through effort and dispassion, and have the objects of their own and lower levels. Abhidh-d_519
The three <s>smṛtyupasthitis</s> (mindful establishments) are considered to be knowledge of others' mental states.
Among the <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power), <s>śrotra</s> (divine ear), and <s>cakṣus</s> (divine eye) superknowledges, the first is <s>smṛtyupasthiti</s> (mindful establishment). Abhidh-d_520

children.text: divyamavyākṛtaṃ śrotraṃ netraṃ cānyā śubhā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: The divine [ear] is morally neutral; the [divine] ear and eye are considered wholesome by others.
The superknowledge that is the fruit of <s>abhijñā</s> [operates] through the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness). Abhidh-d_521
The three <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges) are considered [so] for dispelling confusion regarding the three times;
one is <s>aśaikṣī</s> (of the adept) by nature; the two [others] arise from dependence on the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (adept). Abhidh-d_522
The superknowledges of <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power), [knowledge of others'] minds, and destruction of [outflows] are remembered as the three <s>prātihāryas</s> (miracles).

children.text: harato dve kuśāstṛbhyo mārebhyo harate param // Abhidh-d_523 //
children.translated_text: The [first] two carry away from unwholesome [states and teachers]; the last carries away from <s>Māra</s>. Abhidh-d_523
<s>Samādhi</s> (concentration) is called <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power); its fruit is eightfold sovereignty.
This is twofold as movement and creation; movement is regarded as threefold. Abhidh-d_524
The <s>manomayī gati</s> (mind-made movement) of the Teacher proceeds merely from intention;
for others it is produced by <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve), and thence it carries the body along. Abhidh-d_525
<s>Rūpa</s> (form), <s>gandha</s> (smell), <s>rasa</s> (taste), and <s>sparśa</s> (touch) — creation in the <s>kāma</s> (desire) [realm] is held [to involve these];

children.text: rūpasparśau matau rūpe sveśarīre 'tha vā bahiḥ // Abhidh-d_526 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (form) and <s>sparśa</s> (touch) are considered in the <s>rūpa</s> (form) [realm], either in one's own body or externally. Abhidh-d_526
Through the mind that is the fruit of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), those [creations] are fourteen.
The fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> is two; increasing by one for each higher level above. Abhidh-d_527

children.text: tallābho dhyānavat jñeyaḥ śuddhakācca svataśca tat /
children.translated_text: The attainment of that should be known as like <s>dhyāna</s>; and that [arises] from the pure [dhyāna] and from one's own [level].
Creation is by one's own level alone; but speech [can be] also by a lower [level]. Abhidh-d_528
The speech of these created [beings] is only by the creator alone, except for the <s>Sugata</s> (the Buddha);

children.text: ekasya bruvataḥ sarve nirmitā bruvate samam // Abhidh-d_529 //
children.translated_text: when one speaks, all the created [beings] speak simultaneously. Abhidh-d_529
Having empowered the creation, they speak with another [type of] mind.

children.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ mṛtasyāpi sthirasyaiva tu vastunaḥ // Abhidh-d_530 //
children.translated_text: Empowerment [can apply] even to the dead, but only of a stable [material] object. Abhidh-d_530
One who is undefeatable [cannot be defeated] by many; the victorious ones [are the case] in reverse.
That which arises from <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) is morally neutral; but by birth it is threefold. Abhidh-d_531
For <s>arhats</s>, this sovereignty arises in ten ways,
through the conjunction of the knowledge of the destruction of all <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) and the twofold liberation. Abhidh-d_532
Even sovereignty is similar in this [regard] between teacher and disciple as stated;
but the great difference of the Teacher — that has been declared previously. Abhidh-d_533
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the stability of mind together with its factors; it is fourfold by the distinction of factors.
The designation '<s>dhyāna</s>' is used in the primary sense there, and figuratively for those co-existing with it. Abhidh-d_534
In brief, this fourfold classification of <s>dhyāna</s> has been stated.
I shall now expound the distinctions of its substantial [components] according to scripture. Abhidh-d_535
Together with the fourfold <s>ārūpya</s> (formless [attainments]), <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) is held to be eightfold,
consisting of four or five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), as stated, operating by groups. Abhidh-d_536

children.text: bhedena tu samāpattidravyāṇi daśa sapta ca /
children.translated_text: By distinction, however, the substantial [components] of <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) are seventeen,
together with the eight <s>sāmantakas</s> (preparatory stages), and also with the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate meditation). Abhidh-d_537
These and other distinctions thereof will be explained as enjoined by the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise).

children.text: buddhabuddhestu te sarve tattvenāyānti gocaram // Abhidh-d_538 //
children.translated_text: But all of those truly come within the scope of the <s>Buddha</s>'s intelligence alone. Abhidh-d_538
The fundamental <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) are threefold, by the distinction of <s>sāsvāda</s> (savoring) and so forth;

children.text: tathaiva traya ārūpyā bhavāgraṃ tu dvidhā matam // Abhidh-d_539 //
children.translated_text: likewise the three <s>ārūpyas</s> (formless attainments) are threefold; but <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence) is considered twofold. Abhidh-d_539

children.text: sāmantāni dvidhā sapta prathamaṃ tu tridhā matam /
children.translated_text: The seven <s>sāmantakas</s> (preparatory stages) are twofold; but the first is considered threefold.
The <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate meditation) is likewise threefold; the unafflicted one, however, has a lower basis. Abhidh-d_540
That which is like savoring, accompanied by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), is considered worldly and pure [respectively];
that which has destroyed [defilements] below and above — that is the savored; the supramundane is <s>anāsrava</s> (without outflows). Abhidh-d_541
In the first pure [<s>dhyāna</s>] there are five factors: <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought), <s>sūkṣmatā</s> (subtlety of mind),

children.text: prītiḥ sukhaṃ samādhānaṃ kliṣṭaṃ sukhavivarjitam // Abhidh-d_542 //
children.translated_text: <s>prīti</s> (rapture), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>samādhāna</s> (mental composure); the afflicted [form] is devoid of <s>sukha</s> (bliss). Abhidh-d_542
With inner confidence, there are <s>sukha</s> (bliss), <s>prīti</s> (rapture), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) —

children.text: dvitīye 'ṅgāni catvāri kliṣṭe śraddhā sukhādṛte // Abhidh-d_543 //
children.translated_text: four factors in the second [<s>dhyāna</s>]; in the afflicted [form], <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) [replaces confidence], without <s>sukha</s> (bliss). Abhidh-d_543

children.text: tṛtīye pañcame prajñā smṛtyupekṣā sukhaṃ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third and fifth, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>sthiti</s> (stability);
in the afflicted [form], two factors should be known: <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) that is [neutral] pleasure. Abhidh-d_544

children.text: antye catvāryupekṣe dve samādhiḥ smṛtireva ca /
children.translated_text: In the last, there are four: the two <s>upekṣās</s> (equanimities), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness);

children.text: kliṣṭe dhyāne caturthe tu dve aṅge vedanā sthitiḥ // Abhidh-d_545 //
children.translated_text: in the afflicted fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the two factors are <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and <s>sthiti</s> (stability). Abhidh-d_545

children.text: dravyātmanā daśaikaṃ ca nāmnā tvaṣṭau daśaiva ca /
children.translated_text: In terms of substantial entities there are eleven; but by name there are eighteen.
These factors are enumerated; hence a fourfold analysis is set forth. Abhidh-d_546
And of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) —
in the <s>dhyāna</s> preparatory stages and <s>ārūpyas</s> (formless attainments), the factors are not [formally] established. Abhidh-d_547
Because of the cessation of <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), because of the cessation of inhalation and exhalation,
because of the absence of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) feeling — the last [formless attainment] is called <s>ānejya</s> (imperturbable). Abhidh-d_548
In the first [<s>dhyāna</s>], <s>prīti</s> (rapture), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) [are present]; in the second, without <s>sukha</s> (bliss);
<s>Sukha</s> (bliss) and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) in the third; in the last, only <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) is to be known. Abhidh-d_549
Visual, auditory, and tactile consciousness, as well as that which generates <s>vijñapti</s> (manifestation) —
in whatever level is without <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), from the first [<s>dhyāna</s>] onward, that is morally neutral. Abhidh-d_550
Drawn by the apprehension of the sign of space, that which is called <s>ananta</s> (infinite) mental activity [is proclaimed];
transcending all form, the <s>ārūpya</s> (formless attainment) is designated as <s>ākāśānantya</s> (infinite space). Abhidh-d_551
Likewise, perceiving the unlimitedness of mind, it has the characteristic of <s>vijñānānantya</s> (infinite consciousness);
and again, averse to the infinity of consciousness, it is called <s>ākiñcanya</s> (nothingness). Abhidh-d_552
Fearing the annihilation of that [consciousness], it is designated as <s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñā</s> (neither perception nor non-perception).

children.text: ādau tathā prayuktatvāt tatsaṃjñā vyapadiśyate // Abhidh-d_553 //
children.translated_text: Because it is applied in that way at the beginning, that designation is given. Abhidh-d_553
That which has <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), which is dependent and has a following [character],
a mind with <s>ārya</s> (noble) and non-noble aspects — that is called <s>ānāgamya</s> (the access [concentration]). Abhidh-d_554
Four types of meditators are declared, from the observation of the four <s>dhyānas</s>;
they are those who experience the notions of attainment and failure, decline-prone and so forth. Abhidh-d_555

children.text: dhyātā proktastathā dhyeyaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyānaphalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The meditator is declared, likewise the object of meditation, the meditation, and the fruit of meditation.
Because of the non-establishment [of a self], and because of the stated faults, the fourfold [entity] such as <s>ātman</s> (self) does not exist. Abhidh-d_556
Liberation [comes] from the practice of <s>karma</s> (action), and likewise from the practice of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
because [these] exist when there is engagement, and also because of the comprehension of reality. Abhidh-d_557
<s>Karma</s> (action) here should be known as twofold: meritorious and non-meritorious activities.
Meritorious activity is declared as threefold; <s>virati</s> (abstinence) is said to be of that [same] kind. Abhidh-d_558
<s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), however, should be known as the ultimate, as has been previously stated.
One who pursues something other than this merely chews on a bit [i.e., engages in futility]. Abhidh-d_559
Because they lead to harming others, killing, greed, falsehood, and the like
should be known as causes of lower rebirths, blocking the door to well-being. Abhidh-d_560
Because it teaches what is logically sound, because it protects from suffering, because it instructs about faults,
it is called a '<s>śāstra</s>' (treatise); anything other than this should be known as the speech of the deluded. Abhidh-d_561
The power of <s>mantras</s> of the <s>Pārasīkas</s> (Persians) and others to counteract poison is seen in some cases,
but not in all, because they cannot avert calamities and the like. Abhidh-d_562
The mind is defiled by <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the like, and purified by <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and the like.
Therefore, even a <s>vipra</s> (brahmin) — only one endowed with virtues is liberated. Abhidh-d_563
The pure [meditation] is fourfold: <s>hānabhāgīya</s> (decline-prone) and so forth, in order,
corresponding to inferior, equal, strong, and supreme stainless [qualities]. Abhidh-d_564
That which follows the unstained [levels] of one's own and higher abodes of defilement,

children.text: dve trīṇi trīṇi ca dve vā hānapakṣyādyanantaram // Abhidh-d_565 //
children.translated_text: two, three, three, and two respectively — following upon <s>hānapakṣīya</s> (decline-prone) and the rest in sequence. Abhidh-d_565
The <s>vyutkrāntakasamāpatti</s> (leaping attainment) belongs to the <s>arhat</s> with the <s>akopyadharma</s> (unshakeable quality).
Its practice is twofold in levels: having gone [to a level], with the desire to master the access [concentration]. Abhidh-d_566
By leaping through <s>dharma</s> levels, the eight [attainments] from the pure and so forth are <s>anāsrava</s> (without outflows).

children.text: śuddhakācca tṛtīyaṃ svaṃ niṣṭhā śuddhācca nirmalam // Abhidh-d_567 //
children.translated_text: And from the pure [one attains] the third [as] one's own; the culmination from the pure is the stainless. Abhidh-d_567
The wholesome <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>ārūpya</s> (formless) existences are produced only at one's own level or above.
But one abiding at <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence), not attaining movement and the like, resorts to the stainless. Abhidh-d_568
For a beginner and others attaining <s>dhyāna</s>, only the worldly [type of] cultivation [is possible],
except when the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat) and other [stages] are not attained, [and] in the arising of <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate meditation). Abhidh-d_569
For one free from passion who has not attained the earlier preparatory [stage], likewise,

children.text: viraktasya tu pūrvasya nirmalasyaiva bhāvanā // Abhidh-d_570 //
children.translated_text: and for one detached from the earlier [level], only the stainless cultivation [is possible]. Abhidh-d_570
In the <s>nyāma</s> (certainty) path, in <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge), for a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) in the increase of faculties,
in the path called <s>ānantarya</s> (uninterrupted), and in the path of seeing — there are twelve moments. Abhidh-d_571
And in dispassion toward <s>bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence), excluding the knowledge of destruction,
For a noble one in dispassion toward <s>kāma</s> (desire [realm]), on the last path of liberation,
in the three knowledges and in the three so-called [paths], in the <s>nyāma</s> (certainty) [path], excluding the access [concentration]. Abhidh-d_573
For a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) with passion, in the increase of faculties of the first three levels,
in the preparatory and liberation paths, and for one born from <s>kāma</s> (desire realm) onward in <s>dhyāna</s>; Abhidh-d_574
in the attainment of twofold <s>arhattva</s> (arhatship), on the last path of liberation,
and for detached <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners), the unhesitating ones in the conquest of three levels. Abhidh-d_575
The cultivation of both types [applies]; but there is no cultivation of both [simultaneously].
In the <s>nyāma</s> (certainty) [path] dependent on <s>ānāgamya</s> (access [concentration]), in the arising of that which pertains to it, and so forth. Abhidh-d_576
In the second and subsequent [dhyānas], by this very method, reasoning accordingly,
the cultivation yet to come should be known through knowledge of the <s>Abhidharma</s> method. Abhidh-d_577
The <s>sāsvāda</s> (savoring) [meditation] has [objects of] its own existence; the wholesome <s>dhyāna</s> surveys everywhere;
the wholesome fundamental <s>ārūpyas</s> (formless attainments) do not apprehend the world below. Abhidh-d_578
By the stainless <s>dhyānas</s> and <s>ārūpyas</s> (formless attainments), the defilements of the mind are abandoned;
but [defilements of] lower levels are obtained even by the pure preparatory stages. Abhidh-d_579
Three <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) are declared: with <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), and so forth.

children.text: dhyānāntare sa cārodhaḥ sadvayo 'nyatra nirdvayaḥ // Abhidh-d_580 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate meditation) there is also that suppression; [elsewhere] the pair [exists], or [it is] without both. Abhidh-d_580
With and without <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) and other [distinctions], the three [samādhis] exist in eleven levels.
The <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) beginning with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) illuminate noble aspects. Abhidh-d_581
Ten aspects are of <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness); of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), two are held;
<s>Animitta</s> (signlessness) operates with four aspects of the <s>amṛta</s> (deathless). Abhidh-d_582
For the attainment of the two kinds of <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), the pure [concentrations] again—
those very three are disclosed by the term <s>vimokṣamukha</s> (gateway to liberation). // Abhidh-d_583 //
The three called "further <s>samādhis</s>" are <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness) and so forth;
two take as their object the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (adept's) [path]—from the perspective of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and from <s>anitya</s> (impermanence) respectively. // Abhidh-d_584 //
The last one apprehends <s>kṣaya</s> (destruction), called <s>apratisaṃkhyā</s> [nirodha], from the perspective of <s>śānta</s> (the peaceful);
all [three] belong to eleven planes, are <s>sāsrava</s> (with outflows), and among humans they are without anger. // Abhidh-d_585 //
The cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation): the first, being wholesome, is for the sake of happiness;

those called for seeing, for <s>kṣaya</s> (destruction), and for <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) are said to be for the differentiation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), [cultivated] through effort. // Abhidh-d_586 //
That which is last, in the <s>vajropama</s> (diamond-like) <s>dhyāna</s>, is for the destruction of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements);
and this <s>sūtra</s> was declared by the <s>Buddha</s> as leading to oneself [i.e., for personal realization]. // Abhidh-d_587 //
Of the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables): <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is non-hatred, and likewise <s>kṛpā</s> [i.e., <s>karuṇā</s>] (compassion),
<s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) is delight—of these [three]; <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) is held to be non-attachment. // Abhidh-d_588 //
Of <s>vyāpāda</s> (ill-will), <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness), <s>arati</s> (discontent), and longing-and-aversion respectively—
this is declared as the antidote, for the purpose of taming one's own mind. // Abhidh-d_589 //
<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), being directed toward bestowing happiness, is [associated with] happiness; <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion) faces toward the removal of suffering;

children.text: muditā modanānimnā sattvā ebhyeva paścimā // Abhidh-d_590 //
children.translated_text: <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) inclines toward rejoicing; and the last [<s>upekṣā</s>] concerns these very beings [with equanimity]. // Abhidh-d_590 //
The operation of these should be understood through the aspects [beginning with] 'may they be happy' and so forth;
by even one among these, one attains union with <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>brahmasāyujya</s>). // Abhidh-d_591 //
Among humans, [the <s>apramāṇas</s>] depend on <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm); the one called <s>muditā</s> belongs to two <s>dhyānas</s>;
the others have six planes; some hold [they extend] across seven. // Abhidh-d_592 //
Eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) are taught; of these, the first two have the nature of <s>aśubha</s> (the impure) [contemplation]—
those two belong to the last [stages] of the first two <s>dhyānas</s>; the third is characterized by <s>alobha</s> (non-attachment). // Abhidh-d_593 //
Four <s>vimokṣas</s> called the <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome) <s>ārūpya</s> (formless) [attainments] are [states of] concentration;
the attainment called <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation) is declared as the eighth <s>vimokṣa</s>. // Abhidh-d_594 //
Its direct realization occurs immediately after the subtlest of the subtle [mental states];

children.text: vyutthānacittamapyasyāḥ svaṃ śuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ tvadhaḥ // Abhidh-d_595 //
children.translated_text: the emergence-consciousness from this [attainment] is one's own, pure, and undefiled—but [belongs to the plane] below. // Abhidh-d_595 //
The first three <s>vimokṣas</s> are for seeing objects of <s>kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm) and <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm);
the others, however, belong to the category of inferential knowledge (<s>anvayadhī</s>), observing suffering and so forth in the upper [realms]. // Abhidh-d_596 //
In the <s>sūtra</s>, the eightfold <s>āyatana</s> (base) called <s>abhibhvāyatana</s> (station of mastery) is taught;
this, being an extended practice of the <s>vimokṣas</s>, demonstrates mastery over the mind. // Abhidh-d_597 //
